f2a-3: The last Buffalo variant took on extra fuel (908 L) and some airframe changes without a stronger engine, so its climb, speed and handling all got worse. After a disastrous showing against Zeros at Midway it was pulled from the front line and relegated to training. In the game it is slow and climbs poorly, and with no armour its engine and fuel tanks are exposed, but it turns very tightly with careful flap use and carries four 12.7 mm guns plus two 100 lb bombs for soft targets. It has been available since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
f2g-1: Goodyear's "Super Corsair" combined the Corsair airframe with the 28-cylinder, 3,000 hp Pratt & Whitney R-4360 and a bubble canopy; the F2G-1 was the land-based low-altitude interceptor version. Only ten were completed before the Bearcat, poor test results and engine trouble ended the programme in 1945. In the game it is extremely quick down low and dives and handles superbly, helped by effective flaps, but without a usable high supercharger gear it fades with altitude. Six .50 cal guns, bombs and rockets complete it. It was a Battle Pass Season I reward in Update "New Power".
f2h-2: The Banshee grew out of the late-war XFD-1 Phantom, and the F2H-2 was its most numerous version, with over 300 built; its Westinghouse J34-WE-34 engines gave about 8% more thrust and made room for extra pylons and fuel. In the game it is fast, reasonably agile and very steady at high speed, and a structural limit just under 1,000 km/h lets it dive away from many early jets. Four 20 mm cannons in the nose tear through aircraft, particularly with the air-target belt. It came to the game in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
f3d_1: Douglas beat three rivals to meet a 1945 Navy requirement for a radar-equipped jet night fighter able to fly from carriers, and the XF3D-1 Skyknight flew in 1948; 28 production F3D-1s, with uprated J34-WE-34 engines and around 2,267 kg of added weight, went to the Navy and Marines. In the game it is a flexible multirole aircraft: it turns respectably, its four nose-mounted M3 cannons hold about 16 seconds of fire, and bombs and Tiny Tim rockets let it hit ground targets. The attacker airspawn gives it a useful head start. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
f3f-2: Grumman's F3F, designed in 1934 to cure the F2F's poor spin recovery, was the final biplane adopted by the US armed forces, serving from 1936 until monoplanes such as the Buffalo took over in 1941; 147 of all versions were built. The F3F-2's 950 hp Wright R-1820 Cyclone makes it unusually fast for a biplane, able to dive to roughly 810 km/h before overspeeding, so boom-and-zoom attacks are realistic. Firepower is its weakness: a single 12.7 mm and a single 7.62 mm gun in the nose. It arrived in Update 1.55 "Royal Armour".
f3f-2_galer: This premium F3F-2 represents the aircraft of Bob Galer, a Marine aviator who ditched it in the Pacific while landing on USS Saratoga; he later became a double ace over Guadalcanal, and the wreck, found in 1988 and raised three years later, is now in the National Naval Aviation Museum. It flies just like the standard F3F-2: quick for a biplane, with a dive limit around 810 km/h, but armed with only one 12.7 mm and one 7.62 mm gun. Only the livery and better reward multipliers set it apart. It came with Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
f3h-2: The F3H-2 saved the troubled Demon programme by replacing the unreliable Westinghouse J40 with the Allison J71, and it could fire AIM-7C Sparrows as well as AIM-9B Sidewinders and carry up to 6,000 lb of ordnance; the F-8 and F-4 superseded it, and the last Navy squadron gave it up in 1964. In the game it is still heavy and short of thrust, so it bleeds energy quickly and manages only a few good turns before slowing to a crawl; long dogfights are best avoided. The Sparrows perform poorly, making the Sidewinders the better choice. It was added in Update "Starfighters".
f4d_1: Douglas's Skyray interceptor drew on German high-speed wing research linked to the Me 163 and Alexander Lippisch, and was meant to catch fast new bombers such as the Tu-16; the prototype was built in 1951 and the type left service in 1964 as the F-4 arrived. In the game its large wing gives a strong climb and lets it run at transonic speeds without breaking up, but it bleeds speed in turns and its guns sit in the wings rather than on the centreline. Four AIM-9Bs make it a capable support fighter, though its FFAR rockets share pylons with the missiles. It was a 2022 Summer Quest reward in Update "Danger Zone".
f4f-3: Grumman's Wildcat carried the US Navy through the early Pacific War against the Zero, valued more for toughness and reliability than agility, and Britain flew it as the Martlet II and III. In the game the F4F-3 is a sturdy all-rounder: four 12.7 mm guns and good pilot protection make head-on passes favourable, it dives well and can out-turn many opponents, but its climb rate and top speed are mediocre. It has been part of the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
f4f-4: The F4F-4 introduced Grumman's Sto-Wing folding wings and raised the armament to six .50 cal guns, but ammunition per gun fell from 450 to 240 rounds and the extra weight cut top speed to about 512 km/h; it remained the Navy's mainstay until the Hellcat and Corsair arrived. In the game it is agile, well protected and hard-hitting for its era, yet it cannot outrun its opponents and climbs very poorly, so climbing away from the fight before diving on targets below works best. It has been available since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
f4f-4_martlet_mk4: Britain received 220 Lend-Lease F4F-4Bs in 1941, fitted with a cheaper Wright Cyclone R-1820-40B and a simpler cooling system, and flew them as the Martlet Mk IV until the end of the war. In the game it shares the Wildcat's heavy armament, sturdy airframe, good pilot protection and fast dive, but the weaker engine gives it a noticeably lower ceiling, a slower climb and less speed than the American F4F-4. It was one of the rewards of the 2018 "Good Old S.U.M.M.E.R" event.
f4u-1a: The first Corsair in the US naval line, the F4U-1A introduces the family's inverted gull wing and its handling traits, and has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27. That wing gives it a good roll rate and strong turning at speed, but low-speed turns are only average. Its R-2800-8W radial takes it to about 646 km/h near 6,800 m, though the airframe is fragile against incendiary rounds, so it survives by keeping its speed up and rolling away from threats.
f4u-1a_japan: Japan captured a pair of American Corsairs during the war and restored one to flying condition, and its test pilots were impressed by the construction and performance. The in-game version matches the US F4U-1A apart from its camouflage and the absence of bombs or rockets: fast, pleasant to fly and well armed with six 12.7 mm M2 Brownings and plenty of ammunition. Its water-injected WEP only lasts around seven to eight minutes, so it needs rationing. It has been in the game since the open beta, before Update 1.27.
f4u-1a_usmc: A Marine Corps F4U-1A, from the service where many pilots rated the Corsair far above older types such as the F2A; early examples lacked water injection until retrofits followed. In the game it differs from the standard F4U-1A only by omitting the arrestor hook, saving around 30 kg for a barely noticeable gain in acceleration, and by having no bombs or rockets. It relies on the same strong high-speed handling and familiar weaponry. It was added in Update 1.39.
f4u-1c: Only about 200 F4U-1Cs were built: essentially an F4U-1D with four 20 mm Hispano cannons, the first Corsair to carry them, though American pilots found the guns unreliable, heavy and more than was needed against lightly built Japanese aircraft. In the game it keeps the Corsair's speed and boom-and-zoom strengths, and the Hispanos destroy aircraft with short bursts and work well against ground targets. Before upgrades, though, the cannons jam easily. It is the lowest-ranked cannon-armed Corsair and has been in the game since the open beta.
f4u-1d: Poor forward visibility kept early Corsairs off carriers, so they flew from land with the Marines while the design matured; the F4U-1D (FG-1D when built by Goodyear) added a stronger Double Wasp, racks for bombs and rockets and drop tanks, and was the version that went to sea, with VMF-214 aboard USS Essex from December 1944. In the game it looks almost identical to the F4U-1A and is slightly slower because of extra drag, in exchange for rockets and dive-bombing ability. In the air it is an energy fighter: climb, dive on targets, then extend away on speed. It has been in the game since the open beta.
f4u-4: Added in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.", the F4U-4 is the game's best energy fighter among the Corsairs, accelerating hard and holding its speed well. There is no air spawn, but the climb rate compensates, so it does best by gaining height first and diving on opponents. Six 12.7 mm machine guns lack the punch of the F4U-4B's cannons yet carry enough ammunition to stay dangerous late into a match. Without fuel injection, the engine cuts out briefly under negative G, so pushing over sharply is risky.
f4u-4b: The cannon-armed counterpart of the F4U-4, added in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.", swaps the machine guns for four 20 mm AN/M3 cannons and gains an uprated engine. It keeps the Corsair's speed, energy retention and sharp instantaneous turn, and the extra power allows some vertical fighting against types like the Fw 190 A, though not against Griffon Spitfires or the Bf 109 K-4. Combat flaps work up to about 450 km/h IAS and make it a surprisingly good turner, but the rudder loses authority above roughly 550 km/h, which complicates shots on evading targets.
f4u-4b_vmf_214: This premium F4U-4B represents WE-18 of VMF-214, the "Black Sheep" Marine squadron, which flew two tours in Korea; piloted by Lt. Joe Bibby, it was brought down by ground fire during a raid near Inchon and destroyed with grenades after its crash landing. It plays like the tech-tree F4U-4B: four high-velocity 20 mm wing cannons with generous ammunition handle both aircraft and ground targets, and the R-2800-42W pushes it to almost 700 km/h in level flight. Lowering the landing gear doubles as an airbrake for boom-and-zoom passes. It was sold as an Xbox premium pack in Update 1.79 "Project X".
f4u-6_au-1: Originally designated F4U-6, the AU-1 was derived from the F4U-5 and was the first Corsair built purely for ground attack, with an engine tuned for low altitude, extra armour and more ordnance capacity; the Marines flew it in Korea from 1952 and it was retired in 1957. In the game extra pylons under the fuselage and wings let it carry a far heavier load than other Corsairs. The added weight makes it a poor dogfighter, so air kills are best taken against distracted opponents. It was the reward for the 2020 "Space Race" event during Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
f4u-7: Built to meet France's urgent need for a carrier aircraft, the F4U-7 combined the F4U-4 airframe with the AU-1's ground-attack equipment and was among the last Corsairs produced; the Aéronavale flew it from 1953 to 1964, including over Algeria and Vietnam. In the game it is one of five Corsairs with 20 mm cannons and remains very fast, though it is heavier than the F4U-4 and F4U-4B because of its ordnance provisions. It is effective against both aircraft and ground targets. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
f6f-3: Grumman's Hellcat was the US Navy's answer to the Zero, beating it on speed and altitude while surviving far more damage thanks to a robust airframe and pilot armour; the F6F-5 added a new cowling, an integral bulletproof windscreen, revised ailerons and a stronger tail around the 2,200 hp R-2800-10W. In the game it is a solid multirole fighter with decent handling, strong guns and a choice of bombs, rockets or a torpedo, able to knock out vehicles in ground battles and then hunt bombers. It began as the F6F-3 in the open beta and was remodelled into the F6F-5 in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
f6f-5_france: France acquired around 150 Hellcats between 1950 and 1953 when it was short of modern aircraft to hold its overseas colonies, and although the Bearcat soon displaced it, the type remained a dependable close-support aircraft in Indochina. The French example is identical to the American F6F-5: a heavy R-2800-powered fighter best flown with dives and speed, yet able to turn reasonably when needed. As a striker it can bring two 1,000 lb bombs, HVARs or even Tiny Tim rockets. One of the first US-supplied aircraft in the French tree, it came in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
f6f-5n: A night-fighter conversion of the F6F-5, the F6F-5N carried an AN/APS-6 radar on its right wing and could mount two 20 mm cannons alongside four 12.7 mm guns; the extra weight and drag cost some performance compared with the standard aircraft. In the game the cannons are its main draw, bringing down fighters and bombers quickly with high-explosive belts, and it keeps the full choice of bombs, rockets and torpedoes. It is weak in sustained turns and vertical manoeuvres but handles well at speed, with a structural limit of 803 km/h. It was added in Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai".
f6f-5n_france: France bought 15 F6F-5N night fighters, alongside 124 F6F-5s, between 1950 and 1953 while rebuilding its forces with wartime surplus; this version added an AN/APS-6 search radar to the Hellcat. In the game it is a capable all-rounder, pairing cannons and heavy machine guns with bombs or a single torpedo for ground and naval targets. Neither the airframe nor the engine is outstanding, so it fights best with an altitude or speed advantage gained early in the match, and dogfighting while still carrying ordnance is unwise. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
f7f1: The Navy's twin-engine Tigercat followed the disappointing XF5F Skyrocket and first flew on 2 December 1943; with the Midway-class carriers not yet ready, the first went to the Marine Corps, and only 35 F7F-1s were built before production moved to a two-seat night fighter. In the game it is a classic heavy fighter: very fast and well armed, durable but not agile, best at low to medium altitude and close to teammates. Its high drag lets many fighters catch it in a dive, the climb is middling despite the air spawn, and the engines overheat on automatic controls, so hit-and-run attacks suit it. It was added in Update 1.43.
f7f3: A development of the twin-engine F7F-1 Tigercat, the F7F-3 has stronger engines that let it carry unguided rockets, including three Tiny Tims that can hit ships and bases. It accelerates faster than the original both in level flight and in dives, which suits boom-and-zoom attacks. The armament of four 20 mm AN/M2 cannons and four 12.7 mm Brownings throws out nearly 8 kg of metal per second. This premium was given away during the 2016 Operation S.U.M.M.E.R. event in Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
f8f1: Grumman's Bearcat was built for the best possible climb rate and to operate from small escort carriers. In the game strong acceleration, climb, top speed and energy retention make it a natural energy fighter that should attack from above rather than turn at low speed, and the airframe absorbs plenty of hits, with 20 mm Hispanos and 30 mm guns the main threats. Its weakness is armament: four 12.7 mm M2s with only 1,250 rounds in total, so aimed bursts at the engine or pilot with M20 API-T work best. Tiny Tims, HVARs and bombs give it real ground-attack ability. It has been in the game since Update 1.33.
f8f1b: Designed after Midway on the principle that climb rate mattered most, the Bearcat put the Hellcat's R-2800 into a lighter airframe with a bubble canopy, giving up range and pilot armour; it arrived too late for the Second World War and was soon displaced by jets such as the Banshee, though France flew some in Indochina. In the game the F8F-1B ends the US Navy's single-engine fighter line and often meets jets: nimble, fast and quick to accelerate, it climbs at over 35 m/s on WEP with water-methanol injection once fully upgraded. The hot-running Double Wasp is its weak point and overheats quickly if neglected. It was added in Update 1.33.
f8f1b_france: France received 200 F8F-1B Bearcats as post-war surplus; outdated by 1951, they were still adequate for close air support against the Viet Minh, who had no air force. In the game it is a capable multirole fighter that carries a large load of bombs and rockets while staying competitive against aircraft. The Hellcat's engine in a much lighter airframe gives it more speed and a far better climb than the F4F, F6F or Corsair, so climbing early and diving on slower climbers works well, and its 20 mm cannons deal with large bombers better than machine guns. It came with Update 1.73 "Vive la France".
f8u-2: Known as "The Last Gunfighter", the Crusader is notable for its variable-incidence wing, which tilts up to help at low speed during take-off and landing. In the game the F8U-2 is the first supersonic US naval jet in the tech tree, with good all-round handling, four 20 mm cannons in the nose, AIM-9D Sidewinders on Y-shaped cheek pylons and a belly tray holding 32 FFAR rockets. Countermeasures help against the many missiles it meets, and unlike the later F-8E it has a radar warning receiver, but its wings are fragile, so dogfights need care. It was added in Update "Ixwa Strike".
f9f-2: The first production Panther, the F9F-2 was Grumman's single-seat Model G79 with wingtip fuel tanks and a Pratt & Whitney J42-P-8, a licence-built Rolls-Royce Nene; it completed carrier trials in March 1949 and joined the Navy that May. In the game it is often outclassed by jets such as the MiG-15 or Venom, and its low top speed shows in one-on-one fights, so it works best as a support fighter picking off distracted enemies. Its agility helps it shake pursuers, and its payload options make it an effective fighter-bomber. It was added in Update 1.37.
f9f-5: The F9F-5 reworked the Panther with a longer fuselage and the Pratt & Whitney J48, rated at over 3,000 kgf; more than 600 reached Navy squadrons and fought in Korea, and the Blue Angels flew it until the F9F-8 Cougar replaced it in 1954. In the game it is a reasonable fighter-bomber with decent handling, a wide choice of bombs and four 20 mm chin cannons that are lethal with the air-target belt. Many opponents outclass it, so supporting teammates beats charging in, and while it can turn well in an emergency, doing so drains its energy. It arrived in Update 1.33.
f9f-8: Grumman's last fighter version of the Cougar, the F9F-8 was refined to stall at lower speed and handle better at high angles of attack, with a thinner wing for more speed and a slightly lengthened centre fuselage; around 600 were delivered, but supersonic jets soon made it obsolete. In the game it benefits from those changes and from four AIM-9B Sidewinders, which, though basic, are handy for forcing opponents to waste energy or finishing slow targets. Four 20 mm chin cannons are deadly against fighters, and bombs and rockets add ground-attack options. It was introduced in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
f_100f_china: The two-seat F-100F became the Republic of China Air Force's first supersonic jet when the USAF handed over ten around the 1958 Taiwan Strait Crisis; with F-104s arriving and little air fighting, they mostly flew training, patrol and ground-attack missions until 1984. In the game it carries a heavier ground-attack load than the F-100A but is easy prey for supersonic enemy jets. It has two fewer nose cannons, though the remaining M39s' good ballistics and up to four AIM-9Es keep it a threat. It was a reward from the 2023 Tokushu Heiki event in Update "Sons of Attila".
f_101c: McDonnell's Voodoo revived the cancelled XF-88 escort fighter as a larger, twin-J57 supersonic aircraft able to deliver tactical nuclear weapons, and an F-101A set a world speed record of 1,943.4 km/h in December 1957. The F-101C added a strengthened fuselage and improved controls; only 47 were built, most later becoming RF-101C reconnaissance aircraft used in Vietnam. In the game its straight-line speed is outstanding, reaching Mach 1.5 and holding it for long periods, but a wide turn radius and modest climb make close dogfights a poor idea. It carries four 20 mm M39A1 cannons and no missiles or ordnance. It was added in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
f_102a_greece: Greece received 24 surplus F-102A interceptors, 19 of them single-seaters, in 1969, and flew them without notable incident until Mirage F1s replaced them in 1977. In the game it sits in the Israeli aviation tree and, like the American version, carries no guns; its only weapons are AIM-4 Falcons in heat-seeking and radar-guided forms, which are awkward to use and have no proximity fuse. Its speed and handling are respectable. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
f_102a_late: Convair's delta-winged Delta Dagger nearly lost its contract when the first prototypes, fitted with a weaker J57 instead of the planned J67, could not go supersonic; a redesign with a longer fuselage, new intakes and a larger wing broke the sound barrier in December 1954. Around 1,000 were built, some seeing action in Vietnam, and the type left US service in 1968. In the game it has no cannon and must rely on AIM-4 missiles, both heat-seeking and radar-guided, which are tricky to use and lack a proximity fuse; its speed and agility are reasonable. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
f_106a_1972: Convair's Delta Dart began as the F-102B, a re-engined Delta Dagger that switched to the J75 and needed a reshaped fuselage and intakes; renamed F-106A in 1956, it was delivered from 1959, with 342 built. From 1972 the Six Shooter programme gave some a clearer canopy, a new sight and a 20 mm M61 cannon. In the game it is fast and carries a strong 20 mm cannon and a helmet-mounted display, but its missiles are limited to slow, short-ranged AIM-4s, and it sheds energy quickly, becoming vulnerable below about 750 km/h. It was the reward for the 2025 Sky Guard event.
f_111a: The F-111 began as a joint Air Force and Navy project for a do-everything long-range aircraft, and after a turbulent development that cancelled the Navy's F-111B and the British F-111K it became a USAF strike aircraft; the F-111A was the first of the "Aardvark" family. In the game it was the fastest aircraft available when added in Update "Kings of Battle", but its TF30 engines accelerate poorly and the draggy airframe bleeds energy in any manoeuvre, though it turns well at low speed. Up to fifty bombs, 456 FFARs or a few precision weapons make it a formidable striker. Loading the four outermost pylons locks the wings forward and keeps it subsonic.
f_111c_raaf: Built for the Royal Australian Air Force to replace its Canberras, the F-111C added longer wings, redesigned intakes, stronger landing gear and new radios; 24 were built new and four converted from F-111As, serving from 1973 until 2010 without seeing combat, though they flew reconnaissance over East Timor. In the British tree it plays much like the American F-111F, carrying all-aspect AIM-9Ls, plenty of countermeasures and the Pave Tack pod to guide laser bombs. Its engines are weaker, its choice of guided weapons is narrower and it has no infrared fire-and-forget missiles. It came in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
f_111f: The F-111F "Pacer Strike" was the most successful Aardvark, pairing uprated TF30-P-100 engines with the AN/AVQ-26 Pave Tack system for precision bombing; 106 were built between 1971 and 1976, many based at RAF Lakenheath, and they struck Libya in 1986 and Iraq in 1991 before the F-15E replaced them. In the game it keeps the F-111A's strengths and adds more thrust, AGM-65B, D and G Mavericks, and laser- and infrared-guided bombs via Pave Tack. Six all-aspect AIM-9Ls let it defend itself, and a large countermeasure supply helps against fighters and SAMs. It arrived in Update "Dance of Dragons".
f_117: Lockheed's Nighthawk, ordered in secret in 1978 in response to increasingly capable Soviet SAMs, was the first operational aircraft designed around stealth, with a shaped, radar-absorbent airframe, no radar of its own and subsonic speed to limit its heat signature. It flew over Panama, Iraq and Afghanistan, and only one was lost, over Yugoslavia in 1999, before retirement in 2008. In the game it was the first stealth vehicle, added in Update 2.41 "Firebirds": slow and without air-to-air weapons, it is helpless once spotted visually, but it can slip past enemy radar to deliver laser-guided munitions with precision.
f_14a_early: The two-seat F-14A Tomcat was built to protect carrier groups from Soviet missile-carrying bombers after the failure of the F-111B, entering service in 1974 with the AN/AWG-9 radar and as many as eight missiles, including the long-range Phoenix; its TF30 engines were notoriously unreliable. In the game it was the first fourth-generation fighter and brought active radar-homing missiles with the AIM-54. Superb flight performance, a broad weapons list and the powerful radar make it a top air-superiority choice. Survivability is its weak point, and its hot engines make flares less effective at decoying missiles even out of afterburner. It came in Update "Danger Zone".
f_14a_iriaf: Imperial Iran ordered 80 Tomcats in 1974 to counter Soviet MiG-25R overflights, and 79 had arrived by the 1979 revolution; the IRIAF used them to great effect against Iraq and, cut off by sanctions, improvised weapons such as Hawk-derived missiles and the huge "Yasser" rocket, keeping the fleet flying as the F-14AM to this day. In the game it keeps the F-14A's strong engines, radar and swing wing while adding Iranian Fakour-90 active radar missiles that outrange the AIM-54A, Sedjil semi-active missiles and Soviet R-27Rs, plus Yasser rockets for ground targets. It was the 2024 Persian Tomcat event reward in Update "Seek & Destroy".
f_14b: Grumman knew from the start that the F-14A's TF30 engines would hold it back, and the F-14B finally replaced them with General Electric F110-GE-400s, improving range, top speed and turn rate, alongside new avionics and the AN/AXX-1 Television Camera System for identifying targets. In the game it is a much stronger Tomcat: the GE engines make it far more competitive in dogfights, and it gains AIM-9M Sidewinders, AIM-7M Sparrows and AIM-54C Phoenixes. Paveway II guided bombs also give it useful ground-attack ability. It was added in Update "La Royale".
f_14d: Last of the production Tomcats, the F-14D Super Tomcat combined F110-GE-400 engines with digital avionics, a glass cockpit and the jam-resistant AN/APG-71 pulse-Doppler radar; post-Cold War cuts limited it to 37 new aircraft and 18 conversions, and it flew over Iraq and Afghanistan until the F-14 retired in 2006. In the game the swing wing and strong F110s give it excellent acceleration, and the radar tracks reliably at long range and has an all-aspect mode. AIM-54C+ Phoenixes handle long range and AIM-9Ms close in. Its size and heat signature make it an easy target. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
f_14d_vf_11: This F-14D wears the colours of VF-11 "Red Rippers", one of the US Navy's oldest squadrons, which began converting to the Super Tomcat at NAS Miramar in 1992, flew it in Operations Southern Watch and Desert Strike, was the first to drop JDAMs from a Tomcat over Afghanistan and moved to the Super Hornet in 2005. In the game it flies like the standard F-14D, with strong F110 acceleration, an all-aspect radar mode, AIM-54C+ missiles for long range and AIM-9Ms for close fights. It is a big, hot target, so watching for threats and keeping its tail away from incoming missiles matters. It came in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
f_15a: The F-15 came from the USAF's F-X programme, launched after Vietnam exposed the F-4's dogfighting weaknesses and hurried along when the MiG-25 appeared; the MiG proved less capable than feared, but the Eagle went on to a record of at least 103 air kills without a confirmed loss. In the game it represents a 1994 Air National Guard jet with 240 countermeasures and the APG-63 PSP radar, but no AIM-120A or BOL rails. Strong avionics, IRCCM AIM-9Ms and huge thrust make it lethal at range and capable in a dogfight, though Su-27s, J-11s and Gripens punish it if it gets slow. It was added in Update "Air Superiority".
f_15a_iaf: Israel's F-15As, named Baz ("Falcon"), arrived under Peace Fox I in the late 1970s and scored the type's first air-to-air kill, a Syrian MiG-21, in 1978; Israeli Eagles account for more than 80 of the F-15's 103-plus victories. In the game it plays almost exactly like the American and Japanese Eagles, with one key difference: alongside the AIM-9L and AIM-9M it can carry the Python 3. Keeping speed up is vital, since high-AoA fighters such as the Su-27 and Gripen win slow fights, so it should use its thrust and stable airframe to force fast engagements. It came in Update "Air Superiority".
f_15c_baz_msip: Baz Meshupar ("Improved Baz") is Israel's upgrade of its F-15s from 1998, with domestic electronics and avionics shared with the F-16 Barak that added a helmet-mounted display and active radar-homing missile capability; it remains the country's main air-superiority fighter. In the game it mirrors the American F-15C MSIP II in systems and armament, led by the long-range AIM-120A AMRAAM and backed by IRCCM-equipped AIM-9Ms and excellent handling for closer fights. It has no modern air-to-ground missiles or laser-guided bombs. It was added in Update "Seek & Destroy".
f_15c_golden_eagle: Golden Eagle was a USAF programme launched in 2010 to keep F-15Cs relevant, fitting the APG-63(V)3 AESA radar, a helmet-mounted cueing system where needed and Link 16; most aircraft were done by 2015, and a few remain in service as the F-15EX takes over. In the game it improves on the earlier F-15C with AIM-120C-5 missiles, the AESA radar, BOL countermeasure dispensers and a Sniper ATP targeting pod with better magnification. Its air-to-ground options are still narrow next to the F-15E's, so it is weak in mixed battles. It was added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
f_15c_msip2: Outwardly almost identical to the F-15A, the F-15C initially added little more than fuel; the mid-1980s MSIP II refit brought the APG-63 PSP radar, flares, new engines and conformal tanks, and later upgrades added the AIM-9M, AMRAAM and newer radars before the F-15EX began replacing it. In the game it represents a mid-2000s jet and is among the strongest air-superiority fighters: it flies slightly worse than the F-15A but carries eight active radar missiles, matched only by Japan's F-15J(M), and its HMD can cue both heat-seekers and the radar. Ground attack is its weak spot, limited to unguided bombs and three TV-guided bombs. It arrived in Update "Seek & Destroy".
f_15e: The Strike Eagle replaced the F-111 in the USAF's heavy strike role, building on the F-15B with a strengthened structure, more powerful engines, conformal tanks with extra hardpoints, a full weapon systems officer station and the APG-70 radar, plus compatibility with LANTIRN and laser- and GPS-guided weapons; it entered service in the late 1980s and still flies. In the game it is as good a fighter as it is a bomber, with outstanding acceleration and speed, eight missiles including AIM-9Ms and AIM-120s, plenty of countermeasures and an HMS, plus enough guided and unguided ordnance to wreck a ground team in one sortie. It came in Update "Firebirds".
f_15i_raam: The Ra'am ("Thunder") is Israel's Strike Eagle, with many F-15E avionics replaced by Israeli systems including the AN/APG-70I radar; it first flew in September 1997 and serves with No. 69 "Hammers" Squadron in place of the F-4E Kurnass. In the game its F100-PW-229 engines make it extremely fast, beyond Mach 2 at altitude and matched only by other F-15E variants. A single sortie can mix guided bombs, GNSS-guided bombs and air-to-ground missiles, and its speed suits long-range AIM-120B shots. Heavier and less agile than the F-15A/C, Rafale or Eurofighter, it should choose its close fights carefully. It was added in Update "Firebirds" alongside the F-15E.
f_15j: The F-15J is Japan's licence-built Eagle, produced mainly by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and introduced in the early 1980s to replace the F-104J and F-4EJ, carrying AIM-9 and AIM-7 missiles as well as the domestic AAM-3. In the game it tops the Japanese air tree: a pure air-superiority fighter with high speed and more agility than its weight suggests, able to hold its own against the Su-27 and Gripen. It is also the only aircraft in the game that can carry the AAM-3. It was added in Update "Air Superiority".
f_15j_kai: The F-15J(M) is Japan's MSIP II upgrade of the F-15J, begun in 1987 with F100-PW-220 engines and an AN/APG-63(V)1 radar for AIM-120s, then extended from 2004 with new seats, engines and avionics for the domestic AAM-4; all 102 planned aircraft were finished by August 2014. In the game its main additions over the F-15J are active radar-homing AIM-120 and AAM-4 missiles and a helmet-mounted sight, which with good flight performance make it a very dangerous air-to-air fighter. Like the F-15J, it offers little against ground targets in mixed battles. It arrived in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
f_16a_block_10: The single-seat F-16A was the Fighting Falcon's first production version, and Block 10 kept the F100-PW-200 engine, its most visible change being a grey radome in place of the black one that made the jet easy to spot in mock dogfights; over 150 were built, and Block 1 and 5 aircraft were brought up to the same standard. In the game it is a superb dogfighter with no radar-guided missiles, limited to six AIM-9Ls that have good range but are fairly easy to flare. GBU-8s and Mavericks give it a varied strike load. It came in Update "Apex Predators".
f_16a_block_10_iaf: Israel's Netz is an early F-16A Block 10, built by General Dynamics under the Lightweight Fighter programme and, like the US jets of that block, unable to carry the AIM-7 Sparrow; Israel became the second-largest F-16 operator and scored the type's first air-to-air kills. In the game it is lighter than the Block 15 and 20 and can pull one or two extra G, which makes it one of the best dogfighters around. Its big advantage over the American Block 10 is the Python 3 heat-seeker, at the cost of the GBU-8, while still offering reasonable close air support. It was added in Update "Apex Predators".
f_16a_block_10_netz_mod: This premium Netz represents aircraft "124" of 115 Squadron, the IAF's "Flying Dragons" aggressor unit; other Netz served with 140 Squadron, which took part in Operation Opera against an Iraqi reactor in 1981. In the game it is the tech-tree Netz with 180 countermeasures instead of 60 and the ability to drop GBU-31 JDAMs. It keeps the F-16A's speed, agility and sustained turn, and six Python 3 missiles alongside the AIM-9L make it lethal in close fights. Like every Block 10, though, it has no radar missiles, so its reach at medium and long range is limited. It was added in Update "Hornet's Sting".
f_16a_block_10_norway: Norway was one of four NATO countries that joined the US in the late 1970s to build the F-16A in Europe as a Starfighter replacement, taking 60 F-16As and 12 F-16Bs from Fokker's Dutch line between 1980 and 1984; its early aircraft were later brought up to Block 10 standard and eventually modernised under the MLU programme. In the Swedish tree it is essentially the same jet as the American or Belgian F-16A: fast, quick-climbing and lively, with a decent payload. It handles less well at high speed and has no semi-active radar missiles for medium-range fights. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
f_16a_block_15_adf: When the Air National Guard took over US air defence in the mid-1980s, 270 F-16A/Bs were converted to the Air Defense Fighter standard, gaining AIM-7 Sparrow capability, the AN/APX-109 IFF and a night identification spotlight; once the Soviet bomber threat faded, many were reverted, stored or sold. In the game the ADF's AIM-7Ms give it the medium-range reach earlier F-16As lack, backed by all-aspect AIM-9Ls and the usual superb dogfighting performance. The added electronics weigh around 280 kg, and as an interceptor it carries no air-to-ground ordnance. It was added in Update "Apex Predators".
f_16a_block_15_adf_italy: Italy leased these jets as a stopgap while its Typhoons were delayed: after a Tornado ADV lease ran out in 2003, the "Peace Caesar" deal supplied 34 ex-USAF F-16s, 30 of them ADF fighters and two-seat trainers, which were all returned between 2010 and May 2012. In the game it is identical to the American F-16A ADF, sitting between the earlier F-16As and the F-16C: it fires AIM-7M Sparrows the lighter variants cannot, but lacks the C's newer systems and extra countermeasures. Air-to-ground ability is minimal, though the M61 cannon can still deal with SPAAGs or IFVs. It came in Update "Apex Predators".
f_16a_block_15_belgium: Belgium hosted the main European F-16 production plant under the four-nation deal to replace the F-104G, ordering 116 aircraft; SABCA opened its assembly line in February 1978 and the first Belgian-built F-16A flew that December, with early Block 1 and 5 jets later given the AN/APG-66 radar and raised to Block 15 standard. In the French tree it is effectively the American F-16A: a versatile multirole fighter with excellent acceleration, speed and climb and a fair payload. It is less agile at high speed and lacks the semi-active missiles needed for medium-range combat. It was added in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
f_16a_block_15_ocu_belgium: Belgium kept its SABCA-built F-16As current through the Operational Capability Upgrade, which brought new computers, avionics, weapons and a stronger engine, and after its Mirage 5 upgrade was cancelled it trialled Matra R550 Magic 2 missiles on one OCU jet before budget cuts ended the effort in the early 1990s. In the game this version leans towards air combat, carrying AIM-9M and Magic 2 heat-seekers, while ground work is limited to two AS-30L missiles guided by an ATLIS II pod. It keeps the F-16A's speed, agility and climb but has no HMD and no thermal imager in its pod. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
f_16a_block_15_ocu_thailand: Thailand's Peace Naresuan programme, agreed in December 1987, began with eight F-16A Block 15 OCUs and four F-16Bs delivered from 1988, with further batches arriving until 2005; some of the newest later received the MLU upgrade, though Gripens are now replacing them. In the game, placed in the Japanese tree, it is a genuine multirole jet, carrying AIM-120 AMRAAMs, AIM-9 Sidewinders and Israeli Python 3s for air combat, plus an ATLIS II pod, Paveway II bombs and AGM-65 Mavericks for ground targets. Its only real weakness is reduced agility at high speed. It arrived in Update "Storm Warning".
f_16a_block_20_mlu: Taiwan's F-16A/B Block 20s were approved in the late 1990s, after France had sold it Mirage 2000-5s; to stay within agreements with Beijing about not supplying US-standard equipment, the US delivered a distinct A/B version rather than the F-16C, and it became the backbone of the ROCAF, later upgraded to F-16V standard. In the game it combines F-16A Block 15 MLU systems with an F-16C airframe, giving a dependable multirole fighter with a pulse-Doppler AN/APG-66 radar and modern air-to-air missiles. Mavericks and LDGP bombs let it handle ground targets as well. It was added in Update 2.23 "Apex Predators".
f_16a_block_5_netherlands: The Netherlands picked the F-16 in May 1979 to replace its F-104Gs and NF-5s, with Fokker assembling all 213 Dutch aircraft; the first reached Leeuwarden in June 1979, and Block 5 jets joined the 322nd and 323rd squadrons from 1980 before the 1990s MLU upgrade. In the French tree it has the series' strong speed, agility and easy handling, with AIM-9Ls for air targets and AGM-65B Mavericks for ground ones. High-speed manoeuvring is mediocre, and without medium-range missiles it cannot fight beyond visual range. It was the reward for the 2026 "Workhorse" event.
f_16a_block_72v_china: Taiwan's F-16V upgrade applies Lockheed Martin's Viper package, announced in 2012, to its existing F-16A/Bs, adding the AN/APG-83 SABR AESA radar, new computers and an improved cockpit; the first upgraded wing, locally designated F-16AM/BM, was commissioned in November 2021 with F100-PW-220 engines and AIM-120D capability. In the game the APG-83 locks and tracks quickly, and with long-range AIM-120Ds it dominates at medium and long range, while keeping the Falcon's agility and climb close in. Limited internal fuel needs watching. GBU-53B bombs and AGM-88C anti-radiation missiles extend its strike options. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
f_16aj: The F-16AJ is a proposal rather than a service aircraft: a YF-16-like F-16A that General Dynamics pitched to Japan in the 1980s when the JASDF sought an F-104J replacement, a contest the F-15 won, while the idea of a Japanese F-16 later evolved into the Mitsubishi F-2. In the game it is one of only two fully multirole F-16As, alongside Taiwan's F-16A MLU, and it brought AGM-65 Mavericks to the Japanese tree, giving its pilots precision ground-attack weapons. A modern radar and an armament much like other F-16s make it a strong choice for both interception and strike. It was added in Update "Sky Guardians".
f_16am_block_15_mlu_belgium: Post-Cold War cuts shrank Belgium's F-16 fleet from 116 to 90, and around 70 were upgraded under the Mid-Life Update to F-16AM standard from 1996, gaining new avionics, the AN/APG-66(V)2 radar, AMRAAMs, Mavericks and Paveway bombs; about 40 still serve, others having gone to Jordan and Ukraine. In the French tree it is among the most flexible aircraft available: AIM-120As, low-smoke IRCCM AIM-9Ms and excellent handling for air combat, and for ground work AGM-65D/G Mavericks and GBU-12 and GBU-24 Paveways guided by a LANTIRN pod with a sharp thermal imager. It was added in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
f_16am_block_20_mlu_netherlands: The Dutch F-16 fleet, 213 aircraft assembled by Fokker from 1979, was modernised in the late 1990s to F-16AM/BM Block 20 MLU standard with a new mission computer, colour displays, the AN/APG-66(V)2 radar and AMRAAM capability, and it remained the backbone of the air force until the F-35A arrived. In the French tree it is a flexible fighter-bomber carrying AIM-120Bs and AIM-9Ms on PIDS+ pylons, with Mavericks and JDAMs for ground targets and a Sniper pod whose thermal imager and zoom make guidance easy. It handles very well in close combat, but its air-to-air missile count is limited. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
f_16am_block_20_mlu_norway: Norway's 74 Fokker-built F-16A Block 15s entered service with 332 Squadron in 1980, and the late-1990s MLU programme raised them to F-16AM Block 20 standard with the AN/APG-66(V)2 radar, AMRAAMs and AGM-119 Penguin anti-ship missiles; F-35As began replacing them in the 2010s, and some went to Romania and Ukraine. In the Swedish tree it mirrors the Dutch F-16AM, with AIM-120As and AIM-9Ms on PIDS+ pylons, Mavericks, JDAMs and a Sniper pod, but it is set apart by the Penguin. Agile and capable close in, it still carries relatively few air-to-air missiles. It was added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
f_16c_block_40_barak_2: After the US declined to fund production of Israel's own Lavi fighter, it instead supplied 60 F-16C/D Block 40s in 1988, named Barak II ("Lightning"); Israel fitted them with Elbit avionics, LANTIRN pods, Rafael Derby missiles and JDAM capability, and they flew in nearly every Israeli campaign before the F-16I and F-35I took over long-range strike. In the game it is far more versatile than the Netz and more agile than the MiG-29SMT, with Derby and AMRAAM active radar missiles and low-smoke IRCCM AIM-9Ms for air combat. Ground targets face unguided, laser-guided and satellite-guided bombs as well as SPICE. It was added in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
f_16c_block_50: The Block 50 F-16C answered the weight growth of earlier C models with the General Electric F110-GE-129, which added thrust at all altitudes, and a faster, more reliable Westinghouse APG-68(V)5 radar, along with new ground-attack weapons; the USAF received its first in late 1991 and many were exported. In the game the stronger engine and relatively light airframe make the F-16CM an excellent dogfighter, and its smokeless, IRCCM-equipped AIM-9Ms are very dangerous, especially from behind. It performs well against both aircraft and ground targets. It was added in Update "Sons of Attila".
f_16c_block_52_aesa: PoBIT, the Post-Block Integration Team programme begun in spring 2022, is the USAF's most extensive F-16 upgrade, bringing the Northrop Grumman AN/APG-83 AESA radar, chosen in 2017, to all 608 Block 40/42 and 50/52 jets along with new displays, electronic warfare equipment, communications and Link 16. In the game its key additions over the Block 50 are the AESA radar and long-range, GPS-aided AIM-120Ds, plus a missile approach warner and new RWR, while a new engine and lower weight slightly improve performance. Ground attack is a weak point, with the AGM-65 the only missile on offer. It was added in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
f_16d_block_40_barak_2: Israel's own Lavi fighter was cancelled over rising costs and US opposition, and as compensation the US supplied F-16C/Ds in 1987, followed a year later by an order for 30 more of each under Peace Marble III; the two-seat F-16Ds received extensively revised displays. In the game it is one of the most capable F-16s, using a LANTIRN pod for all-weather strikes with unguided bombs and smart bombs such as the GBU-16. For air combat it carries smokeless, IRCCM-equipped AIM-9Ms and AIM-7M Sparrows for longer shots. It came in Update "Sons of Attila".
f_16i_sufa: Chosen over the F-15I as a cheaper, more versatile way to replace Israel's F-4s, the F-16I is a Block 52 derivative with more than half its avionics replaced by Israeli systems, allowing it to use Python missiles and SPICE bombs; 50 were ordered under Peace Marble V in 1999 and deliveries began in 2004. In the game it gains a better engine and radar, full-coverage missile approach warning, more countermeasures and a wider strike arsenal than the F-16C or Barak II. Fire-and-forget SPICE bombs make it a superb close-support aircraft, but mediocre handling and few air-to-air missiles (AIM-9Ms and AIM-120Cs) limit it in air battles. It was added in Update "Tusk Force".
f_16xl: General Dynamics' SCAMP project, started in 1977 under Harry Hillaker, gave the F-16 a large cranked-arrow wing, informed by NASA research and similar to the J35's, for better supersonic performance, more fuel and extra hardpoints; two converted prototypes flew in 1982. The F-16XL lost the Enhanced Tactical Fighter contest to the F-15E, and both airframes later went to NASA for aerodynamic research. In the game it offers a wide selection of external weapons and greater range while keeping the F-16A's speed and agility. It was the reward for the 2026 "Space Program" event.
f_20a: The F-20 Tigershark was designed as an export fighter for F-5 users barred from buying the latest US jets: essentially an F-5E with a single F404 engine and a radar able to guide AIM-7 Sparrows. Several countries showed interest, but once US export rules were relaxed, buyers chose F-16s or F-15s and no orders came. In the game it handles like a more powerful F-5E and is among the better dogfighters it meets, rewarding good energy and radar management. It bridges the two F-16As alongside it, combining the ADF's Sparrows with the Block 10's guided ground ordnance, and makes a good premium for US progress. It came in Update "Alpha Strike".
f_222_2: The four-engined F.222.2, added in Update 1.73 "Vive la France", is by far the largest and hardest-hitting bomber at the low ranks, outweighing the loaded Italian S.81 even when empty. Its push-pull radials sit close together, so fighters can disable several at once, and its sixteen unprotected wing fuel tanks catch fire easily, after which the wings soon fail. Three turrets, each with a single 7.5 mm Darne gun, can still punish careless attackers. The payload grows to 2,700 kg with upgrades, enough to wreck vehicle columns or bases, and it bombs best from 100 to 500 m.
f_2a: The Mitsubishi F-2, nicknamed "Viper Zero", came from the FS-X programme to replace the F-1: Japan meant to go alone but brought in the US, and from 1988 General Dynamics and Mitsubishi developed it from the F-16C Block 40. In the game its larger wing gives better turning and energy retention than the F-16 at a small cost in top speed, and the J/APG-2 AESA radar scans quickly and identifies modern jets through NCTR. It carries up to eight missiles, four AAM-3s plus AAM-4s or AIM-7Ms, and a broad strike arsenal including anti-ship missiles and JDAMs, but has no helmet-mounted sight. It was added in Update "Leviathans".
f_2a_adtw: Japan launched the FS-X in 1985 to replace the F-1, sharing costs 60/40 with the US and basing it on an enlarged F-16 with Japanese electronics; 94 were built by 2011. Larger, with a bigger tail, AESA radar and Japanese weapons, the F-2 only resembles the F-16 outwardly, and four prototypes went to the Air Development and Test Wing for testing. In the game it can out-turn an F-16 in theory but bleeds energy faster, so long one-on-one fights can go against it. It carries excellent AAM-3s but has no helmet sight, and unlike the standard F-2A it is limited to AIM-7Ms rather than AAM-4s. It came in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
f_47n_25_re_china: After earlier P-47Ds fared poorly in the Chinese Civil War, the Nationalists on Taiwan received 43 ex-Air National Guard F-47Ns around 1953 while waiting for jets; they sank a PLAN gunboat in 1954 and claimed damage to a MiG-15 before being retired in 1955, ending the ROCAF's era of piston fighters. In the game it offers strong high-altitude performance and long endurance, but like other Thunderbolts it is heavy. Flown with care, it is a strong alternative to the P-47D, with a large payload and enough engine power to escape trouble. It was added in Update "Seek & Destroy".
f_4e_aup_greece: Greece ordered 36 F-4Es in 1972 and added ex-US and German aircraft in the early 1990s; from 1997 DASA and Hellenic Aerospace Industry upgraded 39 to the Peace Icarus 2000 (AUP) standard, adding a new HUD and displays, the AN/APG-65GY radar and more weapons, and 16 were still flying in 2026. In the Israeli tree it is much like the German F-4F KWS LV: the ageing Phantom airframe is neither fast nor agile by the standards it faces, and only the good radar and AIM-120 AMRAAMs make up for that. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
f_6c_pakistan: Pakistan became the largest export user of the F-6, China's licence-built MiG-19, after its losses in the 1965 war with India; China donated the first 60 aircraft, deliveries reached 260 fighters and trainers by 1980, and they served well in 1971, later gaining Sidewinders and over 140 other modifications. The in-game F-6C is modelled in its August 1976 form and flies like the J-6A, a powerful, fast-accelerating energy fighter that turns well until compression sets in. AIM-9Ps make it far more dangerous against foes without flares, but it has no countermeasures, little gun ammunition and stiff controls at transonic speed. It was the 2026 "Lion of Peshwar" event reward.
f_86em_greece: Greece's 120 F-86E(M) Sabres were refurbished ex-Canadian CL-13 Mk.4s reworked by North American, arriving from 1954, gaining NATO camouflage in 1964 and giving way to F-5As in 1965. In the Israeli tree it flies almost exactly like the Italian CL-13 Mk.4: the engine is weak, top speed low and the machine guns struggle against other jets, but it turns well at both low and high speed and still accelerates respectably in a straight line. It came with Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
fa_18a: The Hornet grew from Northrop's YF-17, the loser of the Lightweight Fighter contest, which the Navy chose in 1975 to replace the F-4 and A-7; redesigned with McDonnell Douglas, its separate fighter and attack versions were merged into the F/A-18A, which first saw combat over Libya in 1986 and later in the Gulf War. In the game it is a genuinely multirole jet with a broad arsenal, including infrared-guided bombs, and is among the most agile American fighters, helped by its option to disable limits. Few countermeasures, modest speed for a fourth-generation jet and a shortage of modern guided weapons hold it back. It came in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
fa_18a_hug_2_raaf: Worried in the 1990s that its Hornets would be outclassed by the MiG-29, and finding the Typhoon and Super Hornet not yet ready, Australia upgraded its AF/A-18As through the three-phase Hornet Upgrade Program from 1999, which brought new avionics, radar, communications and weapons, including LITENING pods under HUG 2.4; the type served until the F-35 replaced it at the end of 2021. In the British tree it is close to the Finnish F/A-18C: fast and agile, with JDAMs, AIM-9s, AIM-120C-5 AMRAAMs and pylons carrying many countermeasures. It is short of capable air-to-ground missiles. It came in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
fa_18a_raaf: Australia picked the F/A-18A in October 1981 to replace its Mirage IIIs after comparing the F-15, F-16, Tornado ADV and Mirage 2000, building it locally with GAF and CAC and basing it with 3 and 75 Squadrons at Williamtown and Tindal. In the British tree it is a flexible multirole aircraft with a wide arsenal, including infrared-guided bombs, and excellent agility aided by the option to disable limits. Against other fourth-generation fighters it is short on speed, carries few countermeasures and lacks modern guided weapons. It was added in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
fa_18c_early: Early Hornets fell short of the F-14 they were meant to succeed in fleet-defence weaponry and high-speed performance, so a multi-phase upgrade began; its first stage, adding stopgap weapons like the AIM-7P plus new strike stores and sensors, produced the F/A-18C and two-seat D from the early 1990s. In the game this pack premium has a lesser missile fit than the tech-tree version but is still strong everywhere: superb low-speed dogfighting, capable short-range and semi-active missiles, and one of the best sensor suites around, including NCTR. In mixed battles it brings TV-, laser- and GPS-guided ordnance as well as unguided stores. It came in Update "Hornet's Sting".
fa_18c_finland: Finland chose the Hornet in its 1992 competition to replace MiG-21s and J35 Drakens, preferring it to the F-16, Mirage 2000-5, Gripen and MiG-29 on price and upgrade potential, and received 57 F-18Cs and seven F-18Ds between 1995 and 2000; at first they were armed only for air defence, gaining strike capability in upgrades from 2006 to 2016. The in-game version, in the Swedish tree, reflects that pure fighter role: it has no air-to-ground stores but otherwise matches other Hornets, with up to ten AIM-120 AMRAAMs and good agility. Its speed is mediocre. It was added in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
fa_18c_late: Post-Cold War cuts cancelled the A-12 and a naval F-22, and with the F-14 heading for retirement the Navy kept upgrading the F/A-18C, adding AMRAAM integration, new avionics, strike weapons and internal systems; the unofficial "F/A-18C+" or "Late" label covers these packages, and the Marines still fly upgraded legacy Hornets. In the game it caps the US naval line and plays nothing like the preceding Tomcats, relying on excellent dogfighting, strong sensors, NCTR, an HMD, a modern RWR and plenty of AIM-120s. In mixed battles it can dominate the air or deliver GPS-, TV- and laser-guided weapons, and its spawn cost is kept separate from the F-15E's. It came in Update "Hornet's Sting".
fa_18c_late_switzerland: Switzerland bought 26 F/A-18Cs in 1995, receiving them between 1996 and 1999, and a 2007 upgrade added ATFLIR targeting pods and AN/ALR-67(V)3 radar warning receivers; 25 remain in service after one was lost in an accident. In the German tree it matches the American F/A-18C Late except for using the ATFLIR pod rather than the LITENING II. That means fine dogfighting, strong sensors with NCTR and an HMD, enough AMRAAMs to control the sky over small ground maps, and a wide range of guided bombs and missiles. It came in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
fa_18c_mlu_2_finland: Finland's 64 Hornets, bought as pure air-defence fighters between 1995 and 2000, were modernised in two Mid-Life Update phases from 2006 to 2016: MLU 1 brought a helmet-mounted sight, new missiles and avionics and the F/A designation, and MLU 2 added precision ground-attack weapons such as JDAMs. In the Swedish tree it keeps the fighter version's air-to-air strengths while adding satellite-guided JDAMs of several sizes and pylons holding up to 1,280 countermeasures. It lacks more advanced guided air-to-ground weapons. It came in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
fa_18c_switzerland: Switzerland needed to replace its ageing F-5Es and Mirage IIISs, and after comparative trials against the F-16 in 1988 it chose the F/A-18, with most deliveries made between 1996 and 1999; 25 remain in service. In the German tree it offers superb agility and handling, held back by limited speed. Its weapons include AIM-7P missiles, a wide choice of laser-guided bombs and up to four AGM-65 Mavericks. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
fa_18d_late_malaysia: Malaysia bought eight two-seat F/A-18D Hornets in 1993 alongside MiG-29s, deliberately spreading its suppliers; delivered by August 1997, they serve with No. 18 Squadron, flew their only combat missions during Operation Daulat in 2013 and were upgraded by Boeing from 2011 with JHMCS and new IFF. In the Japanese tree it has all the avionics and weapons of the F/A-18C but carries slightly more weight and less internal fuel because of the second seat. A helmet sight, ballistic computer and thermal imaging support a broad mix of AIM-9, AIM-7 and AIM-120 missiles plus guided and unguided bombs and rockets. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
fa_18e_block_2: The Super Hornet began as McDonnell Douglas's "Hornet 2000", a longer, re-engined F/A-18 that reused much of the original's avionics; when the A-X programme collapsed on cost, the Navy chose it over an updated F-14, and it entered service in 1999, later seeing action over Iraq and the Red Sea and spawning the EA-18G. In the game it is a better striker than the F/A-18C Late and carries many AIM-120s and AIM-9Ms, but its handling and performance are disappointing, and Typhoons and Rafales beat it in close fights. It is best used in mixed battles with AGM-65s and Paveway bombs. It was added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
fa_18f_block_2_raaf: Australia ordered 24 two-seat Block II F/A-18Fs in 2007 to cover the gap left by F-35 delays and the F-111C's retirement; delivered from July 2009, they have a 25% larger airframe than the legacy Hornet, F414 engines, more fuel and the AN/APG-79 AESA radar. In the British tree that radar is its key asset, and it carries a heavier load of much the same weapons. It is less agile than smaller Hornets, though strong high-alpha performance and engine power swing the nose round quickly. In mixed battles the ATFLIR pod with AGM-84H missiles or JDAMs lets it strike from outside most SAM ranges. It came in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
fc_20_bis: CANSA's twin-engined F.C.20 answered a 1938 Italian call for a multirole bomber, attacker and escort, but by its first flight in April 1941 the Ca.313 was already in service; the Bis added a shortened nose with a 37 mm cannon plus a pair of heavy machine guns, bomb pylons and a defensive turret, and only ten F.C.20s of all types were built. In the game the nose armament is its strength, effective against aircraft and ground targets alike, backed by two 160 kg bombs and a 12.7 mm rear turret. It is slow, heavy and climbs poorly, and bleeds speed quickly in manoeuvres. It was added in Update 2.1 "New Power".
ffa_p16: FFA began the P-16 in 1947 as a fighter-bomber meant to go supersonic while operating from Switzerland's short airfields; the first prototype flew in April 1955 and soon crashed, the second broke the sound barrier in 1956, but after a pre-production aircraft was lost the government bought more Hunters instead. Export efforts failed, though elements of the design lived on in the Learjet 23, and one example survives in a museum at Dübendorf. In the German tree it is unremarkable in every flight characteristic, with mediocre speed, acceleration, agility and energy retention. Its powerful cannons and AIM-9B missiles are its only clear strengths. It came in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
ffvs_j22_a: With war looming and foreign purchases blocked, Sweden set up a new state factory, FFVS, to build the J 22: a simple steel-framed, plywood-skinned fighter powered by an unlicensed copy of the R-1830, for which licence fees were paid later. Pilots liked its responsiveness and found it could match a J 26 Mustang below 4,000 m. In the game the J22-A is easy to fly while it keeps its speed and stays below that height, holding its own against most fighters, though it needs an energy edge before engaging Spitfires or A6Ms. Its four machine guns need a well-set convergence. It came in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
ffvs_j22_b: Sweden's J 22 came from a new state factory set up because SAAB was fully occupied and foreign fighters could not be bought or delivered in time; its conventional steel and plywood structure, fuselage-retracting main gear and copied R-1830 engine were all chosen for quick building and easy upkeep. In the game the J22-B handles easily below 4,000 m but struggles above that height, much as pilots found in mock fights against Swedish Mustangs. It suits attacks on light bombers such as the Do 17 or Su-2 better than heavy bomber interception, and its four machine guns work best within their set convergence. It was added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
fiat_cr42: This CR.42 sat in the German tree from the open beta until Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica" moved the Italian aircraft to their own nation, and it remains available to players who unlocked it beforehand. For a biplane it is fast, very agile and tough, and its Breda-SAFAT 12.7 mm guns hit hard, best used within 300 m given their low muzzle velocity. Most opponents, such as P-36s and LaGG-3s, are faster and better armed, so it should climb to medium altitude and draw them into turning fights they cannot win. Bombers other than early biplanes are best left alone or attacked at the engines.
fiat_cr42_italy: Fiat's Falco, regarded as the high point of biplane design, replaced the CR.32 and fought well in Spain, beating even I-16 monoplanes; early in the Second World War its agility let it compete with early Hurricanes and Spitfires until faster, better-armoured fighters overtook it. In the game it is quick, agile and sturdy for a biplane, with two Breda-SAFAT .50 cal guns, but nearly everything it meets is faster and better armed. It wins by luring opponents into turning fights at medium altitude; against a disciplined energy fighter it has few answers. It joined the new Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
fiat_cr42_j11: Sweden bought 72 CR.42 Falcos as a wartime stopgap in 1939-1941, adding radios and calling them J11; pilots praised their dogfighting but disliked the low speed, light armament and open cockpits in the Swedish cold, and accidents blamed on poor materials dogged them until retirement in 1945. In the game it is nearly identical to the CR.42, one of the best biplanes available: fast enough to outrun some early monoplanes, quick to climb and armed with two 12.7 mm guns that wreck unarmoured early aircraft. Like most biplanes, though, it has no flaps, retains energy very poorly and has a fragile airframe. It came in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
fiat_cr42_marcolin: This premium CR.42 wears the scheme of Luciano Marcolin, who commanded the night-fighting 377a Squadriglia Autonoma. It arrived as a German starter premium in Update 1.31, gave way to Flegel's Bf 109 A in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", and stays in the German tree only for those who already owned it. It flies like any CR.42: fast, nimble and durable for a biplane, with hard-hitting 12.7 mm Breda-SAFATs best fired inside 300 m. Faster foes such as P-36s and LaGG-3s can be beaten by luring them into turns at medium altitude, while bombers beyond early biplanes are best avoided.
fiat_cr42_marcolin_italy: Fiat's CR.42 modernised the successful CR.32 and is often rated the best biplane of the Second World War, holding its own against early Hurricanes and Spitfires before being relegated to night bombing, ground attack and patrols; Luciano Marcolin, commander of the 377a Squadriglia Autonoma, was a leading pilot of its CN night-fighter version. This gift aircraft moved from the German to the Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica". In the game it is fast, agile and tough for a biplane with strong 12.7 mm guns; it should draw faster P-36s and LaGG-3s into turning fights, and it outlasts I-15s and Gladiators in long dogfights thanks to better energy retention.
fiat_g50_seria2: The German-tree copy of the G.50 serie 2 has been in the game since the open beta; Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica" moved Italian aircraft to their own tree, but it remains for players who unlocked it earlier. The G.50 is the oldest of the Italian early-war trio with the M.C.200 and Re.2000, all three sharing an 860 hp radial and identical armament.
fiat_g50_seria2_italy: Designed under Giuseppe Gabrielli, whose initial gives it its name, the G.50 "Freccia" was Italy's first all-metal monoplane fighter with an enclosed cockpit and retractable undercarriage, begun in 1936 as the air force tried to catch up after the Spanish Civil War. The second production series, about 200 aircraft, opened up the rear of the cockpit to clear exhaust fumes and revised the fuel system and instruments. In the game it is fairly agile and can match many opponents in a turning fight, and its radial keeps it reasonably quick, but it is fragile, prone to fuel fires and lightly armed. It replaced the German-tree version in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
fiat_g50_seria7as: This gift G.50 AS serie 7 has sat in the German tree since the open beta, and although Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica" moved the Italian aircraft into a tree of their own, it stays available to players who unlocked it beforehand. Like the M.C.200 and Re.2000, the G.50 uses an 860 hp radial and the same guns, and it is the oldest design of the three.
fiat_g50_seria7as_italy: The AS (Africa Sahariana) version adapted the G.50 "Freccia" for desert operations with an additional fuel tank aft of the cockpit, a fully retracting tailwheel and sand filters on the fuel and air intakes; many were converted in the field, so production numbers are unclear. In the game it is still the familiar G.50, agile and well powered but lightly armed and very fragile. The extra tank costs a little climb rate and turn time, though not enough to matter much. It replaced the German-tree version in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
fiat_g91_ps: Fiat's G.91 answered a NATO competition for a cheap, light fighter-bomber shaped by Korean War experience, and 756 were built over 19 years for Italy, Germany and Portugal; the pre-series aircraft tested wing slats and disposable wing tanks and lacked later models' reconnaissance and attack equipment. In the game it is a transonic jet, limited to under Mach 0.98, that is very agile but lightly armed and middling in performance against the jets it meets, which makes it a tough first jet. With no air-to-air missiles and modest thrust it suits a support role, though skilled pilots can fly it at the front. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
fiat_g91_r1: The R/1 was the first attack and reconnaissance version of Fiat's light NATO fighter-bomber, keeping the earlier guns and engine but adding three nose cameras and the ability to fire manually guided AA-20 and AS-20 Nord missiles. In the game it is light and nimble, and the missiles give it real flexibility: the AA-20 is hard to steer but useful for last-second head-on shots and for hitting bombers from awkward angles without closing in. Against ground targets the AS-20 is its best option and can destroy most targets if aimed well, with rockets as a backup. It was added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
fiat_g91_r3: Nicknamed "Gina", the German G.91 R/3 is a transonic fighter-bomber, limited to under Mach 0.90, that arrived in Update 1.91 "Night Vision". It is very agile, accelerates well and carries heavy guns, making it a strong all-round jet against the subsonic and transonic aircraft it meets. It follows the Horten 229 in the tree and suits a similar style of play, and it differs only slightly from the other G.91 R variants.
fiat_g91_r4: The R/4 is a ground-attack version of the G.91, here as an Italian premium first sold as a store pack in Update 1.87 "Locked On" and later brought back for Golden Eagles in Update "Red Skies". It carries a competitive strike load of bombs, rockets and HE-warhead guided missiles, plus a choice of AIM-9B Sidewinders or command-guided AA-20 Nords. Top speed is unremarkable and acceleration fair, but excellent roll and turn rates let it bring its guns to bear quickly and evade the clumsier fighters around it, making it best as a support fighter.
fiat_g91_r4_german: Germany's G.91 R/4 premium arrived for Golden Eagles in Update "Starfighters", was sold as a store pack from Update "Ixwa Strike" for a time, and later returned as an in-game purchase. Built for ground attack, it carries bombs, rockets and high-explosive missiles, and can take either AIM-9B Sidewinders or command-guided AA-20 Nords. Compared with the R/3 it trades heavier cannons for lighter machine guns but gains those missiles. Its speed is ordinary and acceleration decent, yet its roll and turn rates are outstanding, so it works well supporting teammates and dodging less agile opponents.
fiat_g91_y: The G.91 Y of 1966 kept the G.91's general shape but was effectively a new design, based on the longer trainer and fitted with two afterburning General Electric J85s for 60% more thrust, though it still could not go supersonic even in a dive; it added two 30 mm DEFA cannons and served only with Italy. In the game it is heavier and less nimble than the G.91 R/4 but faster, with far better acceleration and energy retention. Lacking countermeasures and infrared missiles, it relies on its cannons and AA-20 Nords in the air, and carries more rockets and bombs plus the longer-ranged AS-30 for ground work. It came in Update "Drone Age".
fiat_g91_ys: Offered to Switzerland but never bought, the G.91 YS was a variant of the twin-engined G.91 Y with revised avionics and newer weapons such as AIM-9 Sidewinders. In the game it carries twin 30 mm DEFA cannons in the forward fuselage, like the Super Mystère B2, and up to 4,000 lb of bombs or FFAR rockets for soft targets. It flies very well but has no countermeasures and a mediocre top speed at a level where most fighters are supersonic, so keeping its speed up is essential against missiles and fast MiG-21s and F-104s. It was added in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
firebrand_tf4: Blackburn's Firebrand began in 1940 as a Sabre-engined fleet interceptor but disappointed, and with Sabres reserved for the Typhoon it was re-engined with a Centaurus and, from 1943, reworked as a torpedo strike fighter with larger wings and tail. Torque and a badly placed cockpit delayed carrier clearance until it entered service on 1 September 1945, and 220 were built before the Wyvern replaced it in 1953. In the game it is a strike aircraft first and a fighter second, something like a British IL-2: four fast-firing Hispano Mk.V cannons shred aircraft and soft targets, while torpedoes or bombs handle ships and ground targets. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
firefly_mk1: The Firefly F Mk I sits early in the Fleet Air Arm line and is recognisable by the chin radiator for its Rolls-Royce Griffon; it was one of the first four-cannon fighters available. Its four 20 mm Hispano Mk IIs carry 160 rounds each, enough for repeated attacks on aircraft or ground targets, and it can add pairs of bombs up to 1,000 lb or, once upgraded, eight RP-3 rockets. Weight and size make the initial climb slow, but its two-stage flaps, which slide back to enlarge the wing, give excellent low-speed turning, and a wide, sturdy undercarriage makes it very forgiving. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
firefly_mk4_netherlands: From 1946 the Dutch naval air service bought surplus British Fireflies to fly from the carrier HNLMS Karel Doorman, using them mainly for ground attack against Indonesian forces in the Dutch East Indies; this one wears the markings of '16-44' of VSQ-7. In the French tree it flies like the British Firefly F.Mk.IV: a steady, capable striker with decent cannons and secondary weapons. Enemy fighters can usually catch and out-turn it, so it is best used where friendly fighters already hold the sky. It was added in Update "Seek & Destroy".
firefly_mk5: Fairey Aviation developed the Firefly in 1940 from its Fulmar, and the FR Mk V multirole version of 1948 added hydraulically folding wings and a stronger Griffon 74; 352 were built up to 1956 and flew with the Fleet Air Arm in Korea and the Malayan Emergency. In the game it remains an excellent ground-attack aircraft, carrying enough RP-3 rockets to kill even heavily armoured vehicles. The extra power raises its speed, but agility is little better than before, so it is weak in air combat, and its size and exposed cooling system make it easy to damage. It came in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
fj_4b: The Fury began as a navalised F-86 Sabre, bought as a stopgap after Korea showed the Navy's straight-wing jets were outclassed by the MiG-15; the FJ-4 was a far more thorough redesign, with a thin wing and skins milled from solid alloy, 50% more fuel than the FJ-3 and six underwing stations. In the game the FJ-4B is a capable multirole jet with four 20 mm cannons, bombs from 250 to 2,000 lb, FFAR rockets useful against bombers as well as ground targets, and two or four AIM-9Bs. Unlike the VMF-232 event version, it cannot carry AGM-12B Bullpups. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
fj_4b_agm_12b: This FJ-4B carries the markings of VMF-232 "Red Devils", a Marine squadron that flew the type from 1956 to 1959, deployed aboard USS Bennington during the 1958 Quemoy-Matsu crisis, logged over 10,000 flight hours that year and later gave up its Furies for F-8 Crusaders. In the game it matches the tech-tree FJ-4B, with four 20 mm cannons, bombs up to 2,000 lb, FFAR rockets and four AIM-9Bs, but adds AGM-12B Bullpup missiles that hit hard, though they need steering all the way to the target. It was the main reward of the 2018 Good Old S.U.M.M.E.R. event in Update 1.79 "Project X".
fokker_d21_mod20: This Fokker D.XXI, added in Update "Ixwa Strike", performs much like the D.XXI-3 before it: slow but very agile, with a good climb. Its key change is a pair of 20 mm cannons, which hit very hard against its usual opponents but add weight, cost a little speed, overheat and jam readily and carry little ammunition. Climbing to around 4,000 to 5,000 m early leaves room to dive away when needed. It is stable and beginner-friendly in simulator battles, but its single fuel tank means any leak or fire is likely to be fatal.
fokker_d21_netherlands: Fokker's first monoplane fighter answered a 1934 Dutch request for an affordable modern fighter; the prototype flew in March 1936 with a Bristol Mercury, and with the rival Koolhoven F.K.58 delayed, the D.XXI was adopted, 36 being built in the Netherlands and more under licence in Finland. Dutch D.XXIs fought on 10 May 1940, downing a Bf 109 and several Ju 52 transports, but most were lost within five days. In the French tree its strengths are agility well above most monoplanes and a good climb, against weak armament, no armour and low speed. It came in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
fokker_d21_serie3_finland: The Finnish Fokker D.XXI-3, added in Update "Fire and Ice", is a slow but very manoeuvrable fighter, comparable to the I-16 in favouring agility over engine power. Four light machine guns are enough for most biplanes, though sturdier fighters take longer to bring down. It climbs well, so gaining 4,000 to 5,000 m early pays off, since it is too slow down low to escape most pursuers. It is stable and approachable in simulator battles, but a single fuel tank leaves it vulnerable to leaks and fires.
fokker_d23: Anthony Fokker's private-venture D.XXIII put one engine in the nose and another in the tail in a push-pull layout to clean up the wing and strengthen the armament; the sole prototype, powered by two Walter Sagitta engines, flew in May 1939, but rear-engine cooling problems and bailout risk dogged its eleven test flights before it was damaged in April 1940, captured by the Germans and scrapped in 1941. In the French tree it shares its unusual layout only with the Do 335, and its 13.2 mm machine guns hit nearly as hard as cannons. Speed and manoeuvrability are both mediocre. It came in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
fokker_g1a: Fokker's G.IA "Jachtkruiser" of 1937 was a heavy fighter with two Bristol Mercury VIII engines and twin tail booms, nicknamed the "Grim Reaper" for its firepower; only 36 were airworthy when Germany invaded, yet they were credited with many Ju 52 transports and 14 confirmed air victories. In the game eight nose-mounted 7.92 mm FN machine guns, with plenty of ammunition, give devastating head-on firepower, but its weight demands careful positioning. It can serve as an interceptor or head-on specialist, or as a ground attacker with bombs and strafing runs on light targets. It was added in Update "Seek & Destroy".
fr_1_fireball: Ryan's FR Fireball, the US Navy's first jet-powered aircraft, paired a piston engine with a jet to give the low-speed acceleration early jets lacked for carrier work; only 66 of 1,044 ordered were delivered before cancellation on VJ Day, and structural failures led to its withdrawal in 1947. In the game, as the first mixed-propulsion aircraft, it turns and handles well at medium to high speed and accelerates strongly for its rank. It also inherits the drawbacks of both engine types: poor low-speed handling, a limited top speed and weak energy retention. It came in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
fr_amc_34: The AMC.34, or Renault YR, was an interwar French cavalry tank begun in 1933; twelve pre-series vehicles went through several turrets, ending with a one-man turret and 25 mm gun in Morocco, but it fell short on mobility and armour, led to the AMC.35 and was fully replaced by the H.39 by 1939. In the game it has a two-man crew, a well-protected turret sitting on a flimsy hull and a weak SA34 L/30 gun that reloads slowly and penetrates only 27 mm at point-blank range. It works best at close range with friendly support. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance" and lost its reserve status to the AMD.35 in Update 1.93.
fr_amc_35: Renault's AMC.35 improved the AMC.34 with a two-man APX-2 turret, unusual in French practice, but reliability and armour problems kept it out of service until the remilitarisation of the Rhineland prompted an emergency order that grew to 50 vehicles, which fared poorly when rushed untrained to Sedan in 1940; Belgium also bought the hull with its own 47 mm guns.
