In the game its hull is only slightly better armoured than the AMC.34's, at 25 mm, but the 47 mm gun penetrates 62 mm, and a loader cuts the reload from about seven seconds to about three. The larger turret is an easier target. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amd_35: Panhard's AMD 35 was a four-man, four-wheeled reconnaissance car for the French cavalry, kept as light as possible and capable of 72.6 km/h with a range of about 300 km; captured examples served the Germans as the P204 (f). In the game it pairs a high-penetration 25 mm SA35 L/72 gun with almost no armour, yet it proves surprisingly survivable. It is very fast on roads but struggles uphill and on soft ground, and sharp turns scrub off speed. Using that road speed to reach an ambush position early, then moving after each engagement, gets the most from it. It was added in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
fr_amd_35_kwk39: After 1945 the French army recaptured several Panhards that the Wehrmacht had rearmed with 50 mm guns from the Panzer III, either the L/42 or the L/60, and kept using them. This version carries the 50 mm L/60, giving a fast, nimble wheeled vehicle a hard-hitting, high-penetration gun. Ammunition is limited, so careless shooting runs it dry quickly, and the thin armour leaves it vulnerable to HE rounds and aircraft. It was added in Update "Hornet's Sting".
fr_amd_35_sa35: A few Panhard 178 armoured cars received a 47 mm SA35 gun in 1939 to improve their anti-tank power, and in 1940 Panhard built a single prototype with a rear-facing 47 mm SA37, which fought with the 1er RAM defending a bridge before its crew destroyed it. In the game the gun handles light and medium tanks such as the BT-7 and Panzer III but struggles against heavier uptier opponents. Armour is so thin that heavy machine guns can pierce the sides beyond 500 m, and the wheels cope poorly with rough ground, so road speed is its main defence. It was a "Repair Factory" event reward in Update "Sky Guardians".
fr_aml_90: Panhard developed the AML-90 in the late 1950s for the French Ministry of Defence, replacing the AML-60's 60 mm mortar with a low-pressure 90 mm DEFA gun firing HE and HEAT, and France used it widely for reconnaissance, policing and counter-insurgency. In the game it has essentially no armour, so even heavy machine guns can knock it out, and it survives only through speed and careful positioning. It is best for flanking, harassment, capturing points and supporting teammates, though its HEAT rounds rarely kill in one shot. As a wheeled vehicle it can bog down in rough terrain and prefers flat ground. It was added in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
fr_amr_35_zt3: The AMR.35 improved on the AMR.33 with a bigger engine and better suspension, making it faster and more agile despite added size and weight; its ZT3 sub-variant mounted a 25 mm anti-tank gun, and just ten had been built and issued when France surrendered in 1940. In the game it plays rather like the Soviet ASU-57, offering a quick-firing 25 mm gun, good mobility and armour that only stops rifle-calibre bullets, and it is arguably the best first French vehicle to research. Heavy machine guns and artillery can still destroy it, so it does best flanking opponents it can penetrate. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_10m_acra: Built on the AMX-10P infantry vehicle, the AMX-10M belonged to the 1960s ACRA programme to fire supersonic guided missiles, with about 4 km range and up to 700 mm penetration, from a 142 mm smoothbore; cost, better conventional fire control and the rise of HOT ended it late in testing. In the game its fast missiles are hard to dodge and penetrate the upper front plates of heavies such as the T95, Maus, IS-7 and Object 279, but they need continuous guidance with the vehicle exposed, inviting return fire. The AMX-10P's 20 mm cannon doubles as emergency anti-aircraft defence. It was added in Update "Sons of Attila".
fr_amx_10p: The AMX-10P, one of France's first infantry fighting vehicles, replaced the AMX-VCI from 1968; a 275 hp engine gives it 65 km/h, and its 20 mm GIAT M693 fires the Rh202's ammunition at 740 rounds per minute. About 1,800 were built until 1994, and the design spawned the AMX-10RC and AMX-10M. In the game it fires quickly and offers an APDS belt in a thin, amphibious hull with at most 20 mm of armour. Its 50° elevation limit leaves a blind spot overhead, but dual feed lets it switch belts to ambush light vehicles, or it can scout and flank for its team. It came in Update "Kings of Battle".
fr_amx_10rc: Built by Nexter for armoured reconnaissance, the AMX-10RC has equipped French cavalry since 1981, more than 240 remained in 2021, and Morocco and Qatar also bought it; it shares automotive parts with the AMX-10P but carries a 105 mm medium-pressure gun in a three-man turret without full stabilisation. In the game it is a wheeled sniper and support vehicle with almost no armour. Strong ammunition, thermal sights, a laser rangefinder and a high-zoom scope make it superb at range, and its speed and acceleration let it flank, pick off several tanks and slip back into cover behind smoke if needed. It came in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
fr_amx_13_75: Designed by AMX in 1946 as a light tank that could be air-dropped with paratroopers, the AMX-13 used a rear-mounted oscillating FL-10 turret whose 75 mm SA 50 L/57 was fed from two six-round drums that had to be refilled once empty; it was exported to over 26 countries and spawned more than a hundred variants. In the game it is a fast, low-profile light tank that excels hull-down on the map's edges rather than in head-on fights. The autoloader and quick turret let it knock out several enemies in rapid succession, though its solid shot must be aimed at guns, breeches or ammunition. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_13_75_ss11: This AMX-13 is the standard FL-10 tank with a launcher for four SS.11 missiles above the gun; Nord's SS.11 was one of the first anti-tank guided missiles, in French service from 1956 into the 1980s and steered by joystick against flares on its tail. In the game it plays like the regular AMX-13: very fast and agile but unarmoured, so it suits hit-and-run flanking and sniping. Setting up early ambushes in unexpected places lets the autoloader dispatch several tanks quickly, while the SS.11s handle distant or heavily armoured targets. The main front line is best avoided. It arrived in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_13_90: The AMX-13/90 swapped the 75 mm gun for a larger low-pressure 90 mm CN 90 F2, much as the EBR was later upgraded, to address the French Army's shortage of anti-tank firepower. In the game it is a quick, nimble scout and flanker with a fast reload, but its OCC 60-62 shell leaves the muzzle at only 950 m/s, so long-range shots take skill, and aiming at weak points, ammunition and crew is essential. With no stabiliser it is ill-suited to close fighting, and its thin armour makes strafing aircraft a serious threat. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_13_chaffee: In 1956 the French looked for a cheap way to modernise their ageing M24 Chaffees, and one answer was to put the Chaffee turret on the AMX-13 hull; officially the AMX-US but known to troops as the AMX-13 Chaffee, only a few were built, serving in colonial policing such as in Algeria before becoming driver trainers. In the game it plays much like the AMX-13 (FL11), with the addition of a roof-mounted 12.7 mm M2HB that is useful against aircraft and light vehicles. Its mobility suits ambushing choke points, capturing zones and scouting, while fighting several enemies at once is best avoided. It was added in Update "Starfighters".
fr_amx_13_dca_40: Short of self-propelled anti-aircraft guns after the war, France tried converting existing tank hulls in the 1950s, and this prototype mounted a 40 mm Mle51 gun derived from the Bofors L/70 in a sloped, fully traversing SAMM S-980 turret on the AMX-13 chassis, able to fire straight up. In the game it is a dual-role vehicle: the accurate, fast-firing 40 mm brings down aircraft readily, and its firepower and mobility make it dangerous to lightly armoured vehicles caught early in a match. Belts can be swapped quickly between ammunition types. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_13_fl_11: When France asked in 1952 for its best light tank to be sent to Indochina, the AMX-13's big FL-10 turret and long 75 mm proved unsuited to the jungle, so the hull received the EBR's smaller FL-11 turret, whose shorter gun gave better HE support and saved 1.5 tonnes. The war ended before production, and the first five went to Morocco. In the game it is a fast flanker and scout with very thin armour; the sloped hull front and turret face may stop weak rounds, but little else. Its slow reverse makes regaining cover hard once spotted, so awareness is vital. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_13_hot: This AMX-13 carries six HOT missiles on launchers beside the turret; developed by Nord and Bölkow to replace the SS.11, HOT is a semi-automatic second-generation missile with more range and speed, built in tens of thousands and used in many wars. In the game it shares the regular AMX-13's speed, agility and lack of armour, but faces far tougher opponents than the SS.11 version, so its 75 mm gun often fails to penetrate. The HOT missiles are its real weapon, defeating even the best-protected targets at long range and making it a long-range tank destroyer; the gun is for exposed flanks. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_30: France's main battle tank from the mid-1960s until the Leclerc, the AMX-30 was designed by AMX on the idea that agility would protect it better than heavy armour; it carried a 105 mm Modèle F1 gun and a 720 hp HS-110 diesel, though its transmission was troublesome, and more than 3,500 were built, including licence production in Spain. In the game it follows a doctrine like the Leopard 1's: mobile, with excellent HEAT ammunition, but very thinly armoured and lacking a full two-plane stabiliser. Almost anything can penetrate it, so it should support stronger allies from range, ambushing to disable tracks or crew before retreating. It came in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
fr_amx_30_1972: From 1972 the AMX-30 replaced its coaxial M2HB machine gun with a dual-purpose 20 mm GIAT M693 cannon, elevating from -8° to 40°, to deter light vehicles and helicopters, and all earlier tanks were brought up to this AMX-30B standard. In the game it is otherwise identical to the first AMX-30 and plays the same way: thinly armoured, so best used as a long-range support tank behind stronger teammates, setting up ambushes to knock out tracks or crew before falling back to cover. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_30_ACRA: The ACRA programme, begun in 1961, aimed to give French tanks a supersonic gun-launched missile with the world's first laser guidance; when state funding ended late in testing, GIAT carried on alone, fitting an AMX-30B (1972) with a smoothbore launcher, sight and guidance unit. Trials succeeded by 1974, but cost and the drawbacks of a tank without a conventional gun led France to choose HOT instead. In the game its fast missiles are very hard to dodge and suit large maps, but guiding them all the way exposes the tank to return fire, and corrections at close to medium range are tricky. It came in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
fr_amx_30_auf_1: The AuF1 put a 155 mm autoloading howitzer, with a 30 km range and eight rounds per minute, on the AMX-30 chassis to give the French Army mobile artillery; development began in 1969, the first prototype appeared in 1972 and orders eventually reached 190 vehicles. In the game its huge shells can destroy even the most heavily armoured targets in one hit, and the proximity-fused round can kill light vehicles behind cover. Low muzzle velocity makes long-range shots difficult, so it does best at close to medium distances, and armour so thin that heavy machine guns can destroy it demands careful positioning. It was added in Update "La Royale".
fr_amx_30_b2: Transmission problems prompted the French Army to upgrade its AMX-30s to B2 standard from 1979, adding a new gearbox, the HS-110-S2 diesel, OFL 105 F1 APFSDS ammunition, a laser rangefinder and a gunner's thermal sight; around 700 were converted, entering service from 1982. In the game it is slightly better protected than the AMX-30B but still lacks a full two-plane stabiliser, so firing on the move or after brief stops is unreliable. It suits support, sniping and flanking, avoiding busy urban fights in favour of patient ambushes. Its thermal sight, the only one at its rank, makes spotting enemies much easier. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_30_b2_brenus: With the Leclerc already ordered, France still upgraded a limited number of AMX-30B2s for its rapid reaction regiments, the 1er and 2e Chasseurs, and BRENUS added 112 GIAT BS G2 explosive reactive armour blocks, roughly equal against HEAT to 400 mm of steel at 60°. In the game its weaknesses grow as opponents improve: without solid armour or a two-plane stabiliser it struggles in sudden close encounters, and its better optics still fall short at long range. It does best flanking from concealment and striking from the side rather than fighting in the centre. It arrived in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
fr_amx_30_dca: The AMX-30 DCA mounted the S 401 A turret, with twin 30 mm Hispano-Suiza 831A cannons and an Oeil-noir fire-control system, on the AMX-30B hull, which offered better mobility and room for more ammunition; the guns fired 5- or 15-round bursts at 650 rounds per minute and folded into an armoured box, though optical tracking limited it to daylight and clear weather. In the game one or two 30 mm hits usually down even well-protected aircraft, the radar improves range and accuracy, and its mobility far exceeds the Chieftain Marksman's. It can also pick off lightly armoured vehicles while flanking. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_30_roland: A Franco-German design of the late 1960s, the Roland 1 surface-to-air missile system was accepted by the French Army in the late 1970s, soon followed by the all-weather Roland 2; widely exported, it saw use in the Falklands and the Iran-Iraq War. In the game it shares the fragility of most SPAAs at its level and carries nothing but missiles, leaving it almost defenceless against ground vehicles, even light ones. Its radar is capable but suffers from clutter near trees, so keeping a lock often means sitting in more exposed open ground. It was added in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
fr_amx_30_super: A West German consortium including MTU, Krupp Atlas Elektronik, Wegmann, Diehl and ZF designed the AMX-30 Super upgrade in the late 1980s, adding an 850 hp MTU diesel, automatic transmission, more fuel, improved running gear, MOLF-30 laser fire control, a two-plane stabiliser and gunner thermals; the single prototype, tested in Saudi Arabia, found no buyer. In the game the stabiliser is the big change, finally letting an AMX-30 fight in towns and lead pushes, while the coaxial 20 mm reverts to an M2HB machine gun. Sold as a pack from Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy", it was withdrawn following the 2023 New Year sale, then returned for Golden Eagles in January 2024.
fr_amx_32: AMX and APX developed the AMX-32 in the late 1970s as an export tank for countries with modest budgets, and this second prototype, P2, replaced the first's 105 mm gun with a 120 mm GIAT CN120-25 G1 and gained a reshaped, better-protected hull front, raising its weight to 40 tonnes. In the game it outperforms every earlier AMX-30 variant, with a stronger gun mantlet and excellent ammunition for its rank. It works best from ambush or as a long-range sniper, and with good knowledge of enemy weak spots it can defeat any tank head-on. It was added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
fr_amx_32_105: The AMX-32 P1, unveiled in June 1979, was the first of six prototypes of an AMX-30 development aimed at export customers with limited budgets, copying the spaced armour of the Leopard 1A3 and 1A4 for better protection against guided missiles; no orders ever came. In the game it shares a two-plane stabiliser and gunner thermal sight with the AMX-30 Super, but a weak engine and heavier build leave it less mobile. Its armour is still too thin to stop most opponents' fire, so the reduced mobility narrows its options, and it is best treated as an alternative to the Super. It came in Update "Apex Predators".
fr_amx_40: After the AMX-32 found no buyers, GIAT started the AMX-40 in 1980 as an all-new, low-cost export tank with a lightly armoured hull, good mobility and the 120 mm CN120-25 G1 gun; four prototypes were built between 1983 and 1985, but with surplus tanks flooding the market at the end of the Cold War it was cancelled in 1990. In the game it feels like a much improved AMX-32 P2, with composite frontal armour that allows a somewhat more aggressive approach. Most opponents at its rank can still penetrate it, so that protection is no guarantee. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
fr_amx_50: The AMX-50 grew from Project 141 of 1945, meant to succeed the ARL-44; its oscillating turret arrived in 1949 with a 90 mm gun, two 100 mm prototypes followed, and then demands for a 120 mm gun and the thin hull moved development on to the Surblindé. In the game it pairs the Lorraine 40t's turret and fast-loading 100 mm gun with a sturdier AMX M4-style hull and plays similarly: mobile but thinly armoured, best used on the flanks. The drum empties after a burst, and against tough heavies such as the IS-3 or IS-6, knocking out the barrel buys time for a careful shot. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_50_1950: Developed in 1950 as an intermediate step in the AMX-50 programme, this version mated the hull with the Char 25t's oscillating turret and 90 mm gun, but France already wanted a bigger, longer gun, which led to the Surblindé and Surbaissé. In the game its longer-barrelled 90 mm fires M82 APHE that exceeds 200 mm of penetration, with a four-second autoloader. Combined with excellent mobility, that lets it tear into an unwary enemy's flanks with one-shot potential. Its armour stops little beyond autocannon fire, and rapid shooting can empty the ready rack. It was the Battle Pass Season X "Royal Guard" reward in Update "Apex Predators".
fr_amx_50_foch: Named after Marshal Ferdinand Foch, the AMX-50 Foch was DEFA's heavy 120 mm self-propelled gun on the AMX-50 chassis, meant to support AMX-50 tanks at long range; a 155 mm upgrade was considered but never seriously pursued. In the game its armour shrugs off ordinary AP and APHE but not the HEAT-FS that becomes common around it. It is reasonably agile for its size, but the casemate gun leaves it exposed to flanking light vehicles. The 120 mm handles anything it meets, though early Cold War tanks such as the T-54 and M48 trouble it. It came with the first French ground tree in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_50_surbaisse: Soviet heavy tanks such as the IS-3 and T-10 pushed France in the early 1950s to give the AMX-50 a 120 mm gun and 90 mm of frontal armour, but weight and reliability problems dogged it, and only five complete prototypes were built while the lighter Lorraine 40t was pursued in parallel. In the game the Surbaissé is a heavy tank in name only: its thin armour offers little, but medium-tank mobility lets it flank and surprise opponents with an autoloading 120 mm that fires every six seconds. A rangefinder also makes it an accurate sniper at 1,500 m and beyond, where its armour holds up better. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_50_surblinde: Presented in 1955, the Surblindé was an up-armoured AMX-50 intended as a French heavy tank to rival the Tiger II and IS-2 with better mobility and reliability, but lack of funding, limited cooperation with the US and West Germany and fast-improving anti-tank weapons ended it. In the game it resembles the Surbaissé but is lower and better protected, with an IS-3-like armour layout, and adds a roof-mounted 20 mm MG 151 effective against aircraft and light vehicles. It is heavier, lacks smoke grenades and has no APHE for its powerful gun, though its mobility is decent for a heavy. It was a World War Season 1 reward in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
fr_amx_elc_901: Built on the Hotchkiss CC2 carrier, AMX's ELC was a small, thinly protected tank destroyer conceived in the 1950s to counter Soviet tanks like the T-54 and T-10; its first prototype got the two-man TC901 turret with a low-pressure 90 mm gun in 1956, but lacked a rangefinder until the TC902 turret. In the game it is a tiny, mobile flanker close to the ELC bis, whose gun can win even head-on fights, and its front-mounted engine and transmission can stop some APHE. Thin sides and turret, plus only ±20° of traverse, make side attacks deadly. It was the Battle Pass Season XXII reward in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
fr_amx_elc_bis: The ELC programme, launched in 1955, sought a small, heavily armed, air-portable tank destroyer able to kill any enemy vehicle at 1.5 km; AMX built two prototypes on the Hotchkiss tankette hull, but the project was dropped in 1961 in favour of the AMX-13 family, and the ELC bis now sits in the Saumur tank museum. In the game it is a quick ambusher and flanker, but heavy machine guns can pierce weak spots in the turret front and its reload is only average, so it should pick targets patiently rather than take on several. Its reverse is slow, making smoke useful for escapes. It came in Update "Wind of Change".
fr_amx_m4: Asked in the late 1940s for a 50-tonne medium tank, AMX first proposed a thinly armoured Tiger II-like design, then thickened it to 80 mm at the front and 40 mm on the sides while saving weight with an oscillating turret and new suspension; the 90 mm M4 prototype's 100 mm successor led to the AMX-50. In the game it is the sturdiest French tank of its tier, with a Panther-like hull whose 80 mm front is sloped at about 55°, plus good mobility and gun depression. Its 90 mm SA47, improved over the ARL-44's, is fed by a seven-round autoloader. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_amx_vtt_dca: The AMX VTT/VCI was an AMX-13-based armoured personnel carrier, carrying up to ten troops behind armour up to 30 mm, with around 3,000 built from 1957; to boost its firepower, a single prototype was fitted with an American M45 quad mount of four .50 cal guns, but it was not adopted. In the game the four M2 Brownings are effective against aircraft, and unlike the M16 MGMC it has no cab blocking its forward arc. Three of the four crew sit inside the armoured hull, which helps survivability, but the guns are too weak against most armoured vehicles, so it is purely an anti-aircraft vehicle. It came in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
fr_arl_44: The ARL 44 was designed just before the end of the Second World War, but only sixty were built from 1949 and it was retired by 1953; its long, narrow hull and covered running gear came almost directly from the Char B1 ter, and its petro-electric transmission, making up for a weak engine, needed an elaborate cooling system that stretched the deck beyond the tracks. In the game its armour is too weak for frontline heavy-tank work, though the front resists many rounds, so it plays best as a sniper. Its gun lacks explosive filler and reloads slowly, so shots must target modules and crew. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_arl_44_acl1: This early ARL-44 pairs a First World War-style track run along the hull with sloped armour and a tall profile influenced by the Panther and Tiger II; it carries the original 1944 ACL-1 turret with a 75 mm gun and a 60 mm front plate, later replaced by a 90 mm gun and thicker armour. In the game it plays more like a medium than a heavy tank, with a good gun but limited ammunition types, decent front and side armour that allows some angling, and 10° of gun depression. Its huge silhouette and exposed, thinly protected turret ammunition are its weaknesses. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_arl_44_mod: The Bayard is a variant of France's first post-war heavy tank, the ARL-44, of which sixty were built from 1949 before retirement in 1953, with a narrow Char B1-derived hull and a petro-electric drive needing extensive cooling. In the game it is almost identical to the standard ARL-44, distinguished by a camouflage based on 1939 experimental schemes tested on B1 bis tanks, spare track links on the front hull and a roof-mounted anti-aircraft machine gun. The gun is powerful, but its mobility and protection make close-range fighting risky. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
fr_b1_bis: The B1 bis was the main production B1, ordered in 1937 with a new 47 mm turret gun, a stronger engine and thicker armour; the extra weight cut its range badly, which helped derail several French counter-attacks in 1940, and only 369 of the 1,114 ordered after war broke out were completed. In the game its armour shrugs off most low-penetration guns, but it is slow and its firepower awkward: the quick-firing 47 mm SA35 sits in a slow one-man turret, while the hull 75 mm has narrow arcs and must be aimed with the hull, undermining angling. Dedicated anti-tank guns can still pierce it. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_b1_ter: Hull No. 101 was an original 1929 B1 rebuilt to trial the B1 ter's armour and features; three further prototypes were lost when their ship was bombed on the Gironde, and No. 101 was seized by the Italians after the armistice, its fate unknown. In the game it averages about 75 mm of armour all round, enough to frustrate even dedicated anti-tank guns without angling, making it the strongest tank in its bracket. It shares the B1 bis's slow speed and hull-mounted gun but can anchor a push on its own. Added as a pack in Update 1.75, it has since been sold for Golden Eagles and offered through Warbonds.
fr_bat_chat_25t: Batignolles-Châtillon built two prototypes of the Char 25t in 1954, a 25-tonne tank about twice the weight of an AMX-13, with a 90 mm D.911 APX gun, four crew and a 65 km/h top speed; it was never adopted, though some of its ideas reached later French designs. In the game it has almost no armour, so head-on fights are a mistake, but superb mobility makes it an outstanding flanker, and a decent reverse lets it pull back after firing. Its gun, in a small autoloading rear turret, handles all but the heaviest targets up close and can pick off flanks at range. It came in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
fr_cckw_353_bofors: France received many GMC CCKW trucks through Lend-Lease and turned some into anti-aircraft platforms by bolting a gun to the bed; they served through the war and in Indochina, and the last French CCKWs, mostly fire trucks, retired in 2000. In the game it carries a single 40 mm Bofors and is very vulnerable to machine guns and HE, though six crew let it survive some glancing AP hits. The Bofors' modest rate of fire makes aircraft hard to hit, but its AP round penetrates 72 mm, so it often serves as a makeshift tank destroyer. It came with the first French ground tree in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_char_2c: The Char 2C was developed during the First World War but entered service only after it, becoming the first super-heavy tank in service and the largest operational tank of its era: 69 tonnes, with some of the thickest armour of its day and a crew of twelve. In the game it is a breakthrough tank, too slow to flank and with a low-velocity gun unsuited to long range, but its shells destroy almost anything open-topped or lightly armoured up close. It struggles to penetrate other heavy tanks, and fast enemy light tanks can catch it off guard, so it should stay with teammates. It was added in Update "Sky Guardians".
fr_char_2c_bis: Between 1923 and 1926 one Char 2C was rebuilt at La Seyne as the experimental 2C bis, with a 155 mm Schneider howitzer firing at 200 m/s in a rounded cast turret, stronger Sautter-Harlé engines and no separate machine-gun positions, weighing about 74 tonnes; it was returned to standard after 1934. In the game it plays like the Char 2C but with a very long reload, so every shot counts, and its armour stops few rounds, leaving its twelve crew and roomy hull to absorb damage. The slow shell can destroy even much higher-ranked tanks and can be lobbed like artillery, though that takes practice. It came in Update "Apex Predators".
fr_citroen_kegresse_p4t: The P.7.T AA is an interwar French anti-aircraft half-track carrying four 13.2 mm Hotchkiss Mle 1930 machine guns, added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance". Its three crew are exposed from every angle, so even rifle-calibre machine guns can knock it out and staying hidden is essential. The half-track layout copes with rough ground, but the weak engine makes hill climbs slow, top speed hard to reach and turning on the spot impractical. In return the four guns fire together, giving it more punch than the GAZ-AAA (4M) and making each hit costly for the early aircraft and biplanes it faces.
fr_crotale_ng: The ItO 90M is Finland's version of the Crotale NG short-range missile system, an updated Crotale introduced in 1990 with the VT-1 missile and new sensors, mounted on the Patria Pasi XA-181 6x6; after a successful 1990 prototype, 20 were delivered by 1993 and upgraded in 2007 with a new thermal imager. In the French tree it can reliably hit aircraft out to 12 km with the fast, agile VT-1, which can catch even highly manoeuvrable targets, and its thermal sight helps at night and in poor weather. Its large size, however, makes it hard to hide from aircraft and enemy armour. It came in Update 2.7 "Red Skies".
fr_crusader_mk_2: The Free French received British Crusaders after France lost its own equipment in 1940, with the 1st autonomous tank company operating around ten Crusader IIs and 18 Crusader IIIs. In the game it is a lively short-range light tank: the fast-reloading 2-pounder suits cramped targets with closely packed crews, and a basic vertical stabiliser and fine handling make it fun to drive. It crosses rough ground far better than the A13 cruisers and does not slide after hard braking. With little armour it should avoid open ground and fight from cover or hull-down, helped by a compact turret and very good gun depression. It came in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
fr_cv_9035_nl: Seeking to replace its M113-based YPR-765s and M577s, the Dutch Army preferred the CV90 to the ASCOD in 2003 trials and in December 2004 ordered 184, later 193, CV9035NLs with Swedish-built hulls and Dutch-built turrets, more power and modern electronics; deliveries began in December 2008, and some were later sold to Estonia. In the French tree its key feature is the 35 mm Bushmaster III, a larger development of the CV9030FIN's 30 mm gun, and it differs from the Danish CV9035DK in armour and weight. A thermal imager and good mobility help, but it is thinly armoured and has no ATGMs. It came in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
fr_embt: KNDS showed the EMBT at Eurosatory 2018 as a Franco-German stopgap ahead of the MGCS programme, mounting a Leclerc S1 turret on a Leopard 2A7 hull to prove the two firms could work together; no customers came forward, and the 2022 tank of the same name was a largely new design. In the game the Leopard hull gives far better protection than any Leclerc, at the cost of mobility and handling, while the turret brings the Leclerc's quick autoloader and good optics but no commander's thermal sight. It is limited to French ammunition, whose OFL 120 F1 dart is clearly weaker than the German DM53. It was added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
fr_fcm_36: FCM's light infantry tank lost the 1934 contest to the Renault R35 but impressed enough, with welded construction and a better turret, to be ordered in 1936; complex production kept output slow and costly until it ended in 1940, and the Germans later turned captured hulls into Marder I tank destroyers. In the game it matches the H.35's weak firepower but has 40 mm of sloped armour all round and slightly better mobility, making it more shield than spear. Nicknamed "Cone" for its turret, it left the main research line in Update 1.85 but can still be unlocked once French rank II is reached. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_hotchkiss_h35: Hotchkiss designed the H.35 in 1933 as a cheap but well-protected infantry support tank, its hull bolted together from six cast sections; the army disliked it, but stopping production was politically impossible, so the first 300 were pushed onto cavalry regiments that had no budget for anything else. In the game it is arguably the weakest French ground vehicle: slow, clumsy and armed with a gun that struggles against most opponents. It should keep out of contested areas and support teammates by disabling tracks and modules on enemy tanks. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_hotchkiss_h39: Cavalry demands for more speed led to the H.39, an H.35 with a 120 hp engine in place of the 78 hp unit, a lengthened hull with a taller, flatter engine deck and, progressively, the longer 37 mm SA38 L/35 gun, which could penetrate 30 mm at 1 km. In the game it improves on the H.35 in gun, armour and especially engine power, making it surprisingly quick on flat ground. It is still below average against foreign rivals, and its narrow tracks bog down in mud and cross-country. It is best used as an urban close-support tank, following teammates and waiting for good shots. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_hotchkiss_h39_cambronne: "Cambronne" was an H.39 of the 14e Bataillon de Chars de Combat, part of the 2e Division Cuirassée that fought in the Battle of France in 1940, and this gift version was handed out in the 2017 "Christmas Presents" giveaway. It matches the regular H.39: a better gun, thicker armour and a much stronger engine than the H.35, giving good speed on firm, flat ground. Mud and rough terrain slow it badly because of its narrow tracks, and it remains weaker than most foreign opponents. It works best supporting teammates in towns, picking its moments to fire. It was added in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_jaguar_ebrc: Developed from 2014 by a consortium of Nexter, Thales and Renault Trucks Defense as the successor to the AMX-10RC and ERC Sagaie, the EBRC Jaguar combines a 40 mm CTC cannon with the SICS communication system; the first 20 pre-series vehicles had arrived by December 2021 and 60 by the end of 2023, with 300 planned by 2035. In the game it is a fast, lightly armoured wheeled vehicle with strong firepower: the 40 mm fires effective APFSDS, and four fire-and-forget Akeron MP missiles handle heavier targets. Its speed comes at the expense of protection. It was added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
fr_leclerc_azur: The Leclerc AZUR is an urban-warfare fit for the Tropicalised Leclerc built mainly for the UAE, which already carried an MTU EuroPowerPack, extra fuel, an external auxiliary power unit, a heavy-duty air conditioner, an HL-80 commander's panoramic sight with thermal imaging and a remote 7.62 mm weapon station. AZUR adds explosive reactive blocks along the flanks and slat armour around the engine. In the game this greatly improves protection against HEAT from the sides, but the blocks do little against APFSDS, so care is still needed. The extra weight makes it slightly less agile than earlier Leclercs. It came in Update "Sons of Attila".
fr_leclerc_s1: Named after Marshal Philippe Leclerc de Hauteclocque, who led the Free French 2nd Armoured Division, the Leclerc replaced the AMX-30 as France's main tank from 1992; its long 120 mm CN120-26 gives high muzzle velocity, and a bustle autoloader allows a three-man crew. Nexter built 134 of this first series. In the game it is well protected and survivable overall, but the large gun mantlet is an obvious weak spot through which the breech can be damaged, and close-range fights expose other weak points. Sniping with its fast ammunition and flanking with its mobility suit it best, and a five-second reload keeps it very competitive. It came in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
fr_leclerc_s2: From 1997 the Leclerc Séries 2 replaced the first series on the production line, adding air conditioning for crew and electronics to suit desert service, a front splash guard, a remote hydraulic track tensioner, bolt-on sponson armour and the Iris thermal sight in place of Athos; 176 were built. In the game it is nearly identical to the S1, as its environmental improvements are not modelled. Mobility and the autoloader let it snipe, ambush or respond quickly, and hull-down on a hill it hides most weaknesses apart from the gun breech. Close urban fighting exposes its many hull weak points. It was added in Update 2.1 "New Power".
fr_leclerc_sxxi: The Leclerc Séries XXI introduced a new titanium-containing composite turret front, lighter reactive armour on the bustle, storage bins redesigned for bigger add-on packages, an IFF indicator and the HL 120 commander's panoramic sight with laser rangefinder and Iris thermal imaging. In the game the modular turret front, combining metal, semi-reactive and ceramic layers, resists even the strongest tank rounds, and extra armour under the gunner's sight makes it less likely to lose its gunner. The HL 120 gives it full hunter-killer capability. It came in Update "Winged Lions".
fr_leopard_1a5be: Belgium bought 334 Leopard 1s between 1968 and 1971 to replace M47s, and from 1994 to 1997 converted 132 to the 1A5BE standard developed by SABCA and OIP Land Systems, keeping the 105 mm L7A3 but adding new fire control, thermal sights and turret controls; they served until 2014, including in Kosovo. In the French tree it mirrors the German Leopard 1A5 with a rangefinder and thermal imaging, but has a different gunner's sight, no extra armour or dozer blade, and distinctive storage boxes. Good mobility and optics make it effective at range, though its thin armour protects little. It came in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
fr_leopard_2a4nl: The Netherlands ordered 445 Leopard 2A4NLs on 2 March 1979 to replace AMX-13s and Centurions, with Dutch smoke launchers, FN MAG machine guns, new radios, a periscopic night sight for the driver and minor turret changes; in 1993, 115 went to Austria and the remaining 330 were upgraded to 2A5NL standard. In the French tree it is a well-rounded tank, quick, hard-hitting and solidly protected, though only 16 rounds sit behind blow-out panels and the armour has several weak spots. It differs from the German 2A4 only in its smoke launchers and machine guns. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
fr_leopard_2a4nl_les: This Leopard 2A4NL represents tanks assigned to the Dutch Education and Training Command (OTCo), formed in 2001 after post-Cold War cuts from the army training command founded in 1969. The Dutch bought 445 2A4NLs from 1979 with their own smoke launchers, machine guns and radios. In the French tree it plays like the standard 2A4NL: mobile, hard-hitting and well armoured, but with only 16 rounds protected by blow-out panels and several weak points. A removable camouflage kit of mesh netting and tarpaulin, plus a different paint scheme, sets it apart. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
fr_leopard_2a5nl: In 1993 the Dutch Army decided to upgrade 330 of its Leopard 2A4NLs to the 2A5NL standard, adding the German 2A5's improved protection, thermal sights, electronics, optics and stabilisers while keeping Dutch smoke launchers and FN MAGs; they entered service in May 1997, but the Netherlands gave up its tanks and sold them all by 2011, before a planned L/55 gun could be fitted. In the French tree it is well protected and mobile, and the DM53 round makes it very lethal. Survivability is less impressive, as most weak zones are unchanged and firing to the rear is nearly impossible. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
fr_leopard_2a6nl: Having sold its Leopard 2A5NLs and disbanded its tank force in 2011, the Netherlands changed course in 2015 and leased 18 Leopard 2A6s from Germany, fitting Dutch smoke launchers and machine guns; they serve in the German-Dutch armoured division, and Leopard 2A8s were announced to join them in 2024. In the French tree it is a 2A5 with the longer Rh120 L/55 gun and its better ballistics. The new gun leaves the old problems in place: mediocre survivability, many weak spots and great difficulty firing to the rear. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
fr_lorraine_100: The Canon d'Assaut Lorraine was a light tank destroyer built on the AMX M4 project's chassis, with Veil-Picard pneumatic tyres in place of road wheels that lowered ground pressure and let it keep moving with damaged tracks; begun in 1950 and finished in 1952, it was cancelled in 1953, though the experience fed later Lorraine projects. In the game it is among the most agile tank destroyers in its class, with excellent top and cross-country speed, neutral steering and reverse. Without a turret or real armour it must avoid close fights and frontal assaults, instead flanking early, ambushing and moving after every shot. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_lorraine_155: Lorraine built two prototypes of this fast 155 mm self-propelled gun in 1950 as a spin-off of the CA Lorraine, the Mle.50 with a central casemate and the Mle.51 with a forward one; the CA Lorraine's cancellation and the army's preference for a turreted 155 mm on the Char 25t hull ended it in 1954. In the game the nimble chassis moves easily, the 155 mm howitzer destroys most vehicles, and a 20 mm cannon is handy against aircraft. Its big, thin hull is very vulnerable to HE and strafing, and even an aced crew needs 20 seconds to reload. It was a 2018 WW2 Chronicles reward in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
fr_lorraine_37l: Hurried into being after heavy French tank losses in 1940, this conversion put a 47 mm SA37 anti-tank gun on a Lorraine 37L tractor, but France surrendered before it could be produced. In the game it has a tractor's mobility and no real armour, so it suits patient sniping from behind hills or bushes, where its small size helps it stay hidden. The SA37 penetrates very well for its level, making it a useful anti-tank addition to an early French line-up. It was added in Update "New Power".
fr_lorraine_40t: Developed from the late 1940s as a lighter companion to the AMX-50, the Lorraine 40t used the CA Lorraine chassis, an oscillating turret with a revolver autoloader and a chevron-shaped nose whose angled 45 mm plates matched about 90 mm of protection, with an 850 hp Maybach giving 60 km/h; two prototypes were finished in 1952, but NATO membership and US-supplied M47s ended it. In the game it is the first French vehicle able to penetrate over 200 mm consistently at normal ranges, seven times a minute, with excellent speed, acceleration and climbing. It suits joining light tanks on wide flanks. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_lvt_bofors: France received LVT amphibious vehicles among the US aid it used to rebuild its forces after the war, and in Indochina it fitted some with a 40 mm Bofors, which proved more effective than the original 37 mm thanks to its firepower and rate of fire. In the game the Bofors gives it much more punch than the standard LVT-4, but survivability is poor, especially against the stronger opponents it meets: autocannons penetrate it easily, and only its large crew keeps it going under fire. It was the Battle Pass Season V "River Hunter" reward in Update "Direct Hit".
fr_m10: Free French forces received 227 M10s between 1943 and 1945, fighting in Italy, France and Germany; with the 2nd Armoured Division at Dompaire they helped destroy around 60 German tanks with few French losses, alongside Shermans and US air support. In the game it shares the M4A2's drivetrain but has a more sloped hull and an open pentagonal M5 mount carrying the 76 mm M7 gun, without the muzzle brake of later 76 mm guns. Turret traverse is mediocre and mobility unremarkable, so it is a poor brawler, but its strong gun shines from defensive positions or with allied support. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_m26_pershing: The M26 Pershing arrived too late to matter much in the Second World War, and with 2,212 built the US soon had surplus to lend; France received some but quickly replaced them with M47s, while Belgium kept its own until 1969. In the French tree it departs from fast, light French designs: average in most respects, with armour marginally thicker than the AMX M4's yet still penetrable by many guns. Its 90 mm M82 APHE, with over 137 g of filler, usually kills in one hit, but struggles against thick frontal plates, and HVAP helps only against flat armour. It was added in Update "Kings of Battle".
fr_m36b2_cefeo: After the war France obtained many surplus M36s, and the M36B2 served with the Régiment Blindé Colonial d'Extrême-Orient in Indochina alongside M24 Chaffees, proving effective against fortifications and light vehicles and in direct fire support. In the game it plays almost exactly like the M36 GMC, with armoured turret covers that offer some defence against shell splinters and rifle-calibre strafing, though heavy machine guns and cannon from aircraft still threaten it. New HEAT-FS ammunition lets it tackle well-armoured vehicles reliably at much longer ranges. It came in Update 2.19 "Drone Age".
fr_m3a3_stuart: Free France operated 651 US light tanks, many of them lend-lease M3A3s, with the 2nd Armoured Division the largest user; they mostly scouted, occasionally supported infantry, and served from D-Day until the war ended. In the game it is very fast, nimble and small, which lets it dodge trouble in most situations. The gun penetrates adequately but its ammunition is mediocre, so firepower is unimpressive for its level, and the stabiliser stops working at high speed, making shots on the move difficult. It was added in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
fr_m44: Belgium received several dozen M44 self-propelled howitzers in 1954 as part of its NATO rearmament, keeping them with its artillery until 1967 and in reserve until 1983. In the game it is compact and mobile, with a powerful 155 mm gun firing M107 HE or M110 smoke shells. Thin armour and an open-topped fighting compartment make it easy prey for tanks and aircraft, traverse is limited to 30°, often forcing hull turns to aim, and the long reload favours fighting at range over close quarters. It was added in Update "Storm Warning".
fr_m46_patton: The M46 Patton, developed from the M26 and used heavily in Korea, reached France through NATO aid as a welcome improvement on the underpowered Pershing, but with M47 deliveries already being negotiated only a few were bought; the 2nd Foreign Cavalry Regiment used them mainly for crew training until M47s replaced them. In the game it is fast and agile for a medium, with decent armour, excellent gun depression and a powerful gun firing HEATFS and APCBC, making it adaptable to many ranges and terrains. Unlike the American M46, it has no M304 round. It was a Battle Pass Season XVIII "The Last Legionnaire" reward.
fr_m4a1_sherman: The first French M4A1s went to the 1ère Compagnie Autonome de Chars de Combat, the "Free French Flying Column" that fought at El Alamein with the British Eighth Army and later joined Leclerc's 2ème Division Blindée as part of the 501ème RCC; more arrived as replacements through 1944 and 1945. With no domestic medium tank until well into the Cold War, the M4A1 is the first capable French medium tank in the game. Its 75 mm M3 is effective, its mobility and armour are adequate, and a basic vertical stabiliser helps when stopping abruptly to fire. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_m4a1_sherman_fl_10: In the mid-1950s the French sought a cheap way to modernise and export their Shermans, and instead of reworking the turret they fitted the AMX-13's lighter, less armoured early FL10 turret with its high-velocity 75 mm SA50 L/57; the idea was later applied to Egyptian M4A4s that fought in 1956 and 1967. In the game the autoloader fires every five seconds, enough to destroy several opponents in quick succession, but the armour is weak, so it should flank early rather than trade shots head-on. First sold as a pack in Update "Starfighters", it left the store after the 2021 May sale and returned for Golden Eagles at the 2022 "Bastille Day" event.
fr_m4a3_105_sherman: French armoured divisions, organised much like their American counterparts, used M4A3 (105) Shermans to give infantry direct fire support from a better-protected platform than towed artillery, the 2nd Armoured Division receiving them first in 1944 and the 1st and 5th in 1945. In the game its 105 mm howitzer fires a far more powerful high-explosive shell than the usual 75 mm, very effective against vehicles. There is no APHE, so heavier targets call for HEAT rounds. Performance is otherwise like other Shermans, except that it lacks their vertical stabiliser. It came in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
fr_m4a3e2_sherman_jumbo: Few M4A3E2 Jumbos were built and most went to US units, but France received a number from American surplus after the war, and one served the French 1st Armoured Division as a headquarters tank with the 2nd African Chasseur Regiment. In the game it is a Sherman with much thicker armour, designed as a breakthrough tank: its front resists the Tiger's 88 mm and, well angled, the Panther's 75 mm. Firepower is the weak point, as it keeps the standard 75 mm M3, though that also brings a vertical stabiliser, so it is most effective in close-quarters fighting. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_m4a4_cn_75_50: This upgunned Sherman came from a 1954 Franco-Israeli programme: having judged the AMX-13's 75 mm SA50 L/57 gun good but its armour too thin, Israel decided to fit the gun to its better-protected Shermans, and from March 1956 its ordnance workshops converted the first 50 M4A4s, known there as the M-50. In the game the high-velocity gun penetrates almost anything it meets, but without the M4A1 (FL10)'s autoloader it reloads far more slowly. The M4A4 hull is barely adequate at this level, so the best approach is to take strong ambush positions early rather than push aggressively. It came in Update 1.75 "La Résistance".
fr_m4a4_sherman: Free France received 656 lend-lease Shermans in 1943 and 1944, including 274 new M4A4s landed at Algiers and Casablanca; despite US requests for uniform divisions, the 1ère and 5ème Divisions Blindées kept mixed fleets, and M4A4s served with several regiments of Chasseurs d'Afrique and Cuirassiers. In the game it is the main French wartime medium. Its armour resembles the M4's, with protruding hatches that break the slope of the front plate, a weakness experienced opponents aim for even with the welded add-on plates. The five-engine Chrysler multibank power unit required a hull lengthened by 15 cm. It was added in Update "Starfighters".
fr_m55: Belgium received 50 M55 self-propelled howitzers from the United States in the mid-1950s and was the last country to operate them, until 1975. In the French tree its only real strength is its 203 mm M47 howitzer, whose HE shell carries roughly 23 kg of TNT equivalent and can destroy any tank in the game with a good hit. It carries just ten rounds and reloads very slowly, so every shot matters, and a miss leaves its large, thinly armoured hull at the enemy's mercy. It came in Update "Tusk Force".
fr_marder_clovis: CLOVIS was a Franco-German tank destroyer prototype on the Marder IFV hull, following the DF105, with the better-protected French FL-20 turret of 1984 carrying a 105 mm CN105 G1 gun and a 20 mm CN20 F2 cannon; buyers preferred the cheaper SK-105, and the Marder hull was outdated by the late 1980s. In the game it plays much like the DF105, with good HEAT shells that destroy most armour and a five-second autoloader that lets it win fights against several opponents. The 20 mm is useful against helicopters and light vehicles. It is mobile but poorly armoured, and differs from the German version only in camouflage. It came in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
fr_marder_df_105: Thyssen Henschel developed the DF105 in the 1980s as an export-only light tank, combining a TAM-based hull and a strong engine with an SK-105-style oscillating turret carrying the autoloaded CN105-57 gun; no foreign buyers appeared and it stayed a prototype. In the French tree it is identical to the German version but meets German opponents more often. Armour is so thin that autocannons can knock it out from the front, but excellent mobility in both directions, a five-second reload and a hard-hitting HEAT shell let it destroy even heavily armoured targets from unexpected flanking routes. It was added in Update "Hornet's Sting".
fr_mars_15: Creusot-Loire built the MARS 15 light tank prototype between the 1980s and 1992 with partners including Renk, SAM, Valeo and Baudouin, aiming to replace the AMX-13, a type sold to 35 countries; shown at Satory in 1990 and in upgraded form at Eurosatory 1992, it attracted no orders despite its modular design and was cancelled. In the game it is an excellent scout with high mobility and a low profile, ideal for flanking and spotting for teammates. Its armour is inadequate for close fights, so engaging from the sides works best, and four smoke grenades help it escape and reposition. It came in Update "Ixwa Strike".
fr_msc: The MSC (Mulet Système Complet) was a GIAT technology demonstrator shown in 1986 under France's EPC programme, launched in 1982 after a joint Franco-German tank project collapsed; though not a complete tank, it proved modular armour and an autoloader that cut the crew to three, laying the groundwork for the Leclerc, whose production began in 1991. In the game it brings composite armour, a turret autoloader, blow-out panels, advanced fire control and good mobility. Its lower front plate is vulnerable and its choice of ammunition is limited. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
fr_panhard_ebr_1951: Panhard's 8x8 EBR descended from the pre-war AM 40 P prototype, with drivers at both ends and a 200 hp air-cooled flat-12 under the fighting compartment, so major engine work meant lifting the turret; around 836 of this first model were built from 1951 to 1954, armed with a manually loaded 75 mm SA 49 in an FL 11 oscillating turret. In the game it is fast and agile, ideal for flanking and capturing points, but its low-velocity, inaccurate gun is unreliable at range and even heavy machine guns penetrate it. It should ambush isolated targets and use smoke to escape. It came in Update "Ground Breaking".
fr_panhard_ebr_1954: The 1954 EBR boosted firepower with the FL10A2C oscillating turret and its long 75 mm SA 50 L/57, fed by two six-round drums, plus a strengthened suspension to carry the extra weight; about 279 were built between 1954 and 1956. In the game good optics and the high-velocity gun make it an effective long-range sniper and scout, while its mobility and autoloader let it wipe out several enemies quickly on the flanks. Its solid shot needs to hit barrels, breeches or ammunition, and smoke grenades cover a fast retreat. It was a 2020 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. reward in Update "Hot Tracks".
fr_panhard_ebr_1963: Between 1964 and 1968, 650 EBR Model 1951s were rebuilt with a larger low-pressure 90 mm CN 90 F2 gun to improve the French Army's limited anti-tank capability. In the game it is a quick, fine-handling scout and flanker, but low muzzle velocity and the lack of an autoloader make long-range fights difficult, so success depends on hitting weak points, ammunition and crew, plus good awareness and map knowledge. Better-armed aircraft are a growing threat at this level, and strafing often proves fatal. It was the Battle Pass Season IV "Fearless Voltigeur" reward in Update "Ground Breaking".
fr_pzkpfw_V_panther_dauphine: After D-Day French forces put as many captured German tanks as they could back into service, mostly Panzer IVs but also a few Panthers and Tigers, some Panthers coming from the encirclement at Dompaire; all were replaced soon after the war. In the game it is a Panther G with French markings and no side skirts, the only real difference from the German version being an early gun mantlet that can deflect shots into the hull roof. It has a powerful gun and faster turret traverse than the Panther D, but very poor reverse, so it does best hull-down at long range. It came in Update 1.91 "Night Vision".
